papers.title: Structure of hydroxyapatite coatings produced by electrodeposition on stainless steel and titanium nickelide substrates
papers.abstract: Problem. Hydroxyapatite (HA, chemical formula Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2) is widely used as a biocompatible and bioactive ceramic due to its structural and chemical similarity to the main mineral component of human hard tissues. A disadvantage of hydroxyapatite is its low mechanical properties (strength, crack resistance, and impact resistance), which undoubtedly limits its use as a structural material but not as a bioactive coating on metal implant surfaces. Electrodeposition is one of the most promising methods for forming bioactive calcium-phosphate coatings on metal implants due to the ability to control the composition, structure, and thickness of the coating at low process temperatures. Aim. The aim of this work is to identify patterns in the formation of the composition and structure of hydroxyapatite coatings produced by electrodeposition on 12X18H10T stainless steel and titanium nickelide substrates, and to optimize the deposition modes. Methods. The influence of electrolyte parameters (Ca2+ and PO4 3 ion concentration, pH, H2O2 and NaOH additives), temperature (23–85 °C), potential and deposition time on the stoichiometry, crystallinity, texture and crystallite size of HA coatings was studied using X-ray fluorescence (XRF), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and IR-spectroscopy. Results. It was shown that the brushite phase (CaHPO4·2H2O) is formed at room temperature regardless of the electrolyte composition. Increasing the temperature to 65 °C or higher, when combined with optimization of pH (4.1–6.0) and potential (−1.7…−3.4 V), allows the synthesis of coatings with a composition close to stoichiometric hydroxyapatite. The regimes ensuring the production of single-phase, highly-crystalline HA coatings with a texture coefficient of up to 2.6, which corresponds to the structure most conducive to osseointegration, were experimentally determined. Conclusions. The best coating characteristics (high crystallinity CI=9.1, crystallite size along the c-axis ~70 nm, c/a ratio=0.730) were achieved for the sample synthesized at T=75 °C, pH=5.0, and U=−1.7 V

papers.title: A Phase‐Field‐Smoothed Learning Method for Nonlinear Hyperelasticity Interface Problems
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This article develops a phase‐field‐smoothed learning method for finite‐deformation hyperelasticity interface problems. In the considered problems, different material phases meet at internal interfaces, the elasticity tensor is discontinuous across the interface, and the displacement field is generally only globally regular. These features make standard strong‐form physics‐informed neural networks (PINNs) difficult to train, since automatic differentiation is applied across low‐regularity solution fields and discontinuous material coefficients. The proposed method, denoted by PFS‐PINN, combines phase‐field smoothing with a displacement–stress mixed PINN. The phase‐field network represents the sharp material interface by a continuous order parameter and constructs a smooth approximation of the discontinuous elasticity tensor. The original nonlinear interface problem is thereby converted into a smooth‐coefficient hyperelastic equilibrium problem. The mixed PINN then treats the first Piola–Kirchhoff stress as an independent network output, so that the equilibrium residual contains the first‐order divergence of the stress rather than second‐order derivatives of the displacement. For the phase‐field‐smoothed problem with continuous coefficients, the convergence of the system energy of the mixed PINN approximation is proved, and an ‐error bound for the displacement is also obtained. Numerical tests cover constant and continuously varying coefficients as baseline cases, and several hyperelastic interface problems with regular, high‐curvature, and multiple interfaces. The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method possesses superior accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness, which constitutes a valuable attempt for addressing complex hyperelasticity interface problems.

papers.title: The Upper-Limb Residual Limb as a Biological Control Interface: Surgical Preparation, Myoelectric Signal Optimization, Rehabilitation, and Neural Prosthetic Integration—A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Upper-limb prosthetic performance depends not only on the mechanical and computational capabilities of the device but also on the quality, selectivity, stability, and accessibility of biological signals available within the residual limb. Methods: A structured narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, IEEE Xplore, targeted Google Scholar searches, and citation chaining was conducted through 11 August 2026. The final synthesis included 111 publications and examined muscle architecture, intervening soft tissues, nerve management, electromyographic control, rehabilitation, surgically created interfaces, implanted sensing, osseointegration, and sensory feedback. Results: Particular attention is given to an earlier developmental research line involving myoelectric acquisition, personalized training, residual-muscle redistribution, fascial signal transmission, nerve mapping, and implantable neural sensing, which is critically contextualized against independent contemporary evidence. Exploratory residual-limb surgical approaches are distinguished from interventions with stronger clinical support. Conclusions: On this basis, we propose the concept of interface-conscious upper-limb amputation: the preservation, organization, accessibility, training, and longitudinal adaptability of the biological structures required for present and future prosthetic control. This framework is not a validated surgical protocol, but a clinically oriented synthesis intended to connect amputation surgery with rehabilitation, neuroprosthetics, and long-term technological evolution.

papers.title: From Campus Learning to Leadership Aspiration: The Role of Higher Education and Experiential Learning in Shaping Women Leaders in Indonesia
papers.abstract: As women's participation in higher education is increasing, their representation in leadership positions is still limited, especially in Indonesia. This study examines how educational design, including classroom pedagogy, co-curricular engagement, and experiential learning, can shape female students' leadership aspirations. This qualitative study is based on Social Cognitive Career Theory and Transformational Learning Theory. The analysis applied a systematic thematic coding procedure, supported by code-frequency mapping, theme co-occurrence analysis, and researcher triangulation, in order to strengthen the transparency and rigor of the analysis. The findings show that gender-inclusive learning climates, active learning methods such as discussions and presentations, and micro-leadership roles within group assignments can improve leadership self-efficacy and identity formation. Co-curricular and experiential learning opportunities can serve as mastery experiences, which can strengthen confidence and relational leadership skills. However, cultural expectations and family norms still influence how women translate their educational experiences into leadership ambitions. This study highlights the role of higher education and also digital and interactive learning environments as spaces that can support inclusive leadership development in non-Western contexts.

papers.title: Accelerating unsupervised near-field acoustic holography via frequency-domain parameter transfer
papers.abstract: Near-field acoustic holography (NAH) enables sub-wavelength sound field reconstruction but demands repeated inverse solutions across hundreds of frequency bins in broadband engineering tests. Unsupervised physics-informed neural networks avoid pre-constructed training datasets, yet their frequency-by-frequency optimization leads to computation times that scale linearly with the number of bins. This paper proposes DP-PINN+, which exploits the analytic continuity of the NAH transfer function with respect to frequency to transfer converged network weights between adjacent bins as warm-start initializations. A normalized transfer-function distance is introduced as an offline metric for assessing transfer feasibility. Online convergence detection adaptively terminates training when the loss improvement rate drops below a preset threshold, and a drift-detection mechanism resets the transfer chain when accumulated bias exceeds tolerance. Simulations over 100–5000 Hz (491 bins) at signal-to-noise ratios of 10, 20, and 30 dB show that DP-PINN+ reduces the average per-bin computation time from 23.78 s to 2.34 s while achieving a broadband-averaged normalized mean squared error of −27.43 dB at 30 dB SNR, with a lower mean NMSE than the baseline physics-informed method and the supervised convolutional neural network. Ablation experiments indicate that parameter transfer primarily provides computational acceleration, whereas DIP mitigates noise-overfitting bias during sequential transfer at low SNR. Sound-insulation measurements on a glass-panel window demonstrate a 4.36× speedup while maintaining numerically comparable reconstruction accuracy under the investigated experimental configuration.

papers.title: Research on state of health prediction of lithium-ion batteries based on sparrow algorithm and dynamic physical constraint neural network
papers.abstract: To address the limitations of insufficient model generalization under small-sample conditions, empirical dependence of physical priors, and inadequate characterization of nonlinear degradation features in the state of health (SOH) prediction for lithium-ion batteries, this paper proposes a hybrid prediction framework fusing the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) and dynamic physics-informed neural network (PINN), termed SSA-PINN-GRU-Attention. Firstly, SSA is employed to globally optimize the parameters of the double-exponential degradation model for constructing adaptive physical prior boundaries. Secondly, a gated recurrent unit combined with the self-attention mechanism (GRU-Attention) is introduced to strengthen the modeling capability for long-term temporal dependencies and local capacity regeneration phenomena. Finally, a dynamic physical constraint weight strategy based on the Huber loss is designed to achieve effective collaboration between physical laws and data-driven learning. Experimental results under leave-one-out validation on the NASA and CALCE CS2 datasets demonstrate the strong cross-battery and cross-dataset generalization capability of the proposed model. The mean e R 2 ,a root mean square error ( e RMSE ), and a mean absolute error ( e MAE ) are 0.9754, 1.3128%, and 0.8014% on the NASA dataset, and 0.9894, 1.2676%, and 0.9873% on the CALCE dataset, respectively. The proposed model also outperforms the representative Double-Exp, PI-GPR, and Dynamic PINN baselines.

papers.title: Involving Live Animals in Science Education: Exploring Cross-Border Practices among Slovenian-Language Primary Schools in Slovenia and Italy
papers.abstract: Involving live organisms into the educational process is recognized as one of the most effective strategies for younger children to acquire scientific knowledge about animals and develop positive attitudes to them. The described approach provides benefits that extend well beyond science education. Previous research has shown the need for further study of the demographics of educational practices involving animals in various international contexts. Our aim was to determine the current ways this approach is practiced in science lessons at Slovenian-language primary-level schools in Slovenia and Italy. Atotal of 208 primary school teachers completed an online survey, with the majority of responses revealing no significant differences between the two countries. Overall, most teachers reported not including live animals in their lessons at all, while those who employ this approach do so very rarely. The reasons most frequently stated for involving animals were to make students more motivated, encourage their active learning, and develop empathy and respect for living beings. Teachers perceived the biggest barriers to implementing this approach as organizational constraints, concerns with hygiene or allergies, and financial costs. Notably, over one-third of all respondents self-assessed their knowledge of appropriate methodological approaches for including live animals in lessons as very poor or poor. Most teachers stressed the need for training programs on this topic, along with systemic regulation that encompasses professional assistance and suitable conditions for integrating animals into the curriculum. Our results indicate that teachers’ knowledge of methodological approaches, animal care and breeding, as well as animal biology, forms a crucial foundation for incorporating live animals in the educational process.

papers.title: Conceptual study of a supercritical CO2-cooled, triply periodic minimal surface lattice-based microreactor
papers.abstract: Advancements in additive manufacturing (AM) processes have made it increasingly feasible to consider optimized shapes such as triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices for heat transfer applications, ranging from heat exchanger designs to nuclear fuel elements. This study introduces a TPMS-lattice-shaped nuclear core and compares its performance against that of a traditional pin-based design. A publicly available design that relies on typical fuel pin elements for a fast spectrum, supercritical CO 2 (sCO 2 )-cooled reactor with a direct Brayton cycle was selected as the reference design. The same core materials were used in the TPMS core to ensure a fair comparison between both geometries. Due to the complexity of this type of geometry, innovative modeling strategies were introduced. The thermal performance of the TPMS fuel element was analyzed using a computational scheme that combined high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with Multiphysics Object-Oriented Simulation Environment (MOOSE)-based 1D thermal hydraulics, coupled with 3D heat transfer. Monte Carlo reactor physics analyses using unstructured meshes in Serpent were employed to characterize the core performance and verified against a native constructive solid geometry TPMS lattice implementation in OpenMC. When it comes to fast spectrum reactors, TPMS geometries are neutronically equivalent to pin geometries. However, TPMS-based fuel elements offer improved heat transfer performance, enabling the power density to be increased up to 59% while still meeting the peak material temperature requirements. A downside of TPMS lattices is the additional pressure drop per unit length, which may be manageable when factoring the pumping power costs into the total energy generated by the proposed microreactor concept.

papers.title: GiziLens Application for Toddler Nutritional Status Classification Using SMOTE-NC and Bayesian-Optimized Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Stunting is a chronic growth disorder in toddlers. Its detection is often hampered by limited conventional diagnostic methods which process the indicators of weight-for-age (W/A), height-for-age (H/A), and weight-for-height (W/H) in a fragmented manner, potentially limiting the understanding of multiple nutritional conditions in toddlers. To address this issue, this research aims to develop GiziLens, a web-based decision support system that integrates the TabNet deep learning architecture using three target-specific models trained separately but executed concurrently on the web application backend to simultaneously produce predictions for the three nutritional status indicators. This study contributes by applying TabNet optimization to local data to handle extreme class imbalance, while transforming it into a practical diagnostic tool. In its implementation, this research utilized 40,071 toddler anthropometric medical records (aged 0–59 months) from Jeneponto Regency for the 2021–2024 period. The class distribution imbalance in the dataset was mitigated using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique for Nominal and Continuous (SMOTE-NC) to regenerate minority samples until reaching a controlled residual ratio, followed by automatic optimal hyperparameter tuning using Bayesian Optimization through the Optuna framework. The evaluation results demonstrated that TabNet produced a tighter train-test generalization gap compared to MLP (0.32% vs 1.60% for W/A; 1.33% vs 2.06% for H/A; and -0.63% vs -3.56% for W/H). The TabNet model achieved a test accuracy of 96.46% (F1-weighted 0.96) for W/A, 95.88% (F1-weighted 0.96) for H/A, and 98.11% (F1-weighted 0.98) for W/H. The developed GiziLens prototype proved technical feasibility and promising retrospective predictive performance as an initial decision support system prior to conducting prospective clinical trials. The GiziLens prototype holds the potential to assist healthcare workers and program managers at Public Health Centers in accelerating integrated early stunting detection, despite the system was designed as an initial decision support instrument and cannot yet replace independent clinical diagnoses.

papers.title: Robustness of Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Against Feature-Space Evasion Attacks for Spam Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract. Email spam filters may classify unmodified messages accurately yet remain vulnerable to deliberate feature manipulation. Hyperparameter optimization can improve predictive performance, but clean-data gains do not by themselves characterize behavior under test-time perturbations. A controlled evaluation is therefore needed to assess both properties within the same leakage-controlled protocol. Purpose: This study compared the clean classification performance and feature-space robustness of a library-default Random Forest (RF-default) and a Bayesian-optimized Random Forest (BO-RF) on Spambase. Methods/Study design/approach: Exact duplicates were removed and predictor-identical records were grouped to prevent cross-fold leakage. The models were evaluated using two repetitions of five-fold nested stratified group-aware cross-validation with shared outer folds. Bayesian Optimization maximized inner-validation spam-class F1. Frozen outer-test folds were assessed on clean inputs, class-center-directed perturbations at α = 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, and 0.40, and 30 magnitude-matched random directions. Retained inference covered clean-versus-directed and directed-versus-random contrasts in F1, Recall, and model-specific attack success rate (ASR). Result/Findings: BO-RF achieved 95.01 ± 0.66% clean Accuracy compared with 94.92 ± 0.74% for RF-default; its mean clean Precision, Recall, and F1 were also slightly higher. Directed perturbations progressively reduced performance. At α = 0.40, Accuracy was 89.24% for RF-default and 89.32% for BO-RF, while Recall declined to 77.94% and 78.03%, respectively, indicating increased false negatives. Directed ASR reached 15.470% and 15.484%, and relative F1 degradation reached 8.915% for both models. All 24 clean-to-directed comparisons and all 24 directed-versus-random comparisons for F1, Recall, and ASR met the Holm-adjusted threshold. Novelty/Originality/Value: The study combines duplicate-aware nested evaluation, shared folds, and identical perturbation settings to examine clean optimization and directed feature-space degradation in one paired protocol. Findings are restricted to the evaluated feature-space setting.

papers.title: Rethinking Mathematics Classrooms in Higher Education
papers.abstract: Within the scope of the Applied Mathematics course taught at the School of Technology and Management of the Polytechnic Institute of Bragança, an active learning methodology was implemented, incorporating key elements such as: Continuous and constructive feedback during classes; Annual adaptation of the methodology based on student suggestions; Group-based learning, promoting collaboration and social comfort; A safe environment for questioning, essential for teaching advanced mathematics; Diversification of assessment tools, ensuring fairness and inclusion; Integration of international students, with flexible use of languages and bilingual materials; Encouragement of the conscious use of Generative Artificial Intelligence tools; Use of collaborative digital platforms that promote transparency, co-authorship, and resource sharing. This pedagogical practice fosters skills associated with the Individual Development Goals, such as autonomy, critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration, while also aligning with European standards. This practice not only promotes academic success but also actively contributes to students’ personal, professional, and scientific development, creating a solid foundation for lifelong learning and their integration into an increasingly demanding and technology-driven job market.

papers.title: Satellite–6G and Geospatial Sensor Fusion for Quantum-Secure Carbon Measurement, Environmental Digital Twins and Global Climate Intelligence
papers.abstract: Abstract: Climate mitigation increasingly depends on carbon measurements that are spatially explicit, temporally frequent, auditable and resilient to cyber-physical . Existing satellite, terrestrial sensing, digital-twin and mobile-network solutions remain fragmented, while emerging 6G and low-Earth-orbit infrastructures create both an opportunity for continuous environmental intelligence and a new security surface. This paper proposes a model-based architecture that integrates Earth-observation satellites, terrestrial geospatial sensors, 6G/LEO connectivity, uncertainty-aware multimodal fusion, environmental digital twins and quantum-resilient trust controls for carbon measurement, reporting and verification (MRV). The methodological contribution is the Satellite–6G Quantum-Secure Environmental Digital Twin Intelligence (S6Q-EDTI) framework. It combines matrix state estimation, dynamic digital-twin updating, constrained multi-objective optimization, Bayesian uncertainty propagation and a risk-adjusted climate-intelligence score. The literature supplied for the study supports the feasibility of GIS-based environmental digital twins, secure 5G/6G twins, LEO routing, sensor-fusion architectures, quantum/post-quantum communications and Earth-observation analytics (Rusnák et al. 2026; Khan, Qureshi & Abd Malek 2026; He et al. 2026; Miao et al. 2026). An illustrative 0–10 numerical example yields a composite system score of 8.55/10 under assumed weights, while explicitly avoiding claims of empirical validation. The paper further develops an invention-oriented architecture and draft claim concepts centered on cryptographically verifiable provenance, cross-layer fusion, adaptive routing and uncertainty-bounded carbon estimates. The proposed approach provides a coherent foundation for scalable carbon MRV, environmental digital twins and planetary-scale climate decision intelligence, subject to future field validation, standards alignment and jurisdiction-specific legal review. Keywords: Satellite–6G integration; geospatial sensor fusion; carbon MRV; environmental digital twin; climate intelligence; low-Earth-orbit networks; post-quantum cryptography; quantum-secure communications; Earth observation; Bayesian data fusion; uncertainty quantification; provenance; edge intelligence; climate-risk analytics; digital-twin orchestration.

papers.title: Quantitative Scale‐Invariant Analysis of Fracture Surface Roughness in Very‐High‐Cycle Fatigue of LPBF‐Manufactured 316L Stainless Steel
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The very‐high‐cycle fatigue behavior of 316L stainless steel produced by laser powder bed fusion was investigated using a multitechnique approach combining infrared thermography, nonlinear acoustic monitoring, X‐ray computed tomography, and quantitative fractography. The primary aim of this study was to establish quantitative links between process‐induced defect characteristics, damage accumulation mechanisms, and fracture surface morphology in the very‐high‐cycle fatigue regime. The fatigue limit was determined via the Risitano–Luong thermographic method (285 ± 10 MPa) and validated by conventional S–N curve analysis (260 MPa). Tomography identified elongated fusion‐related defects (mean size 26 μm, maximum 157 μm) that may have acted as internal crack nucleation sites, leading to subsurface‐initiated cracking with characteristic «fish‐eye» morphology. Scale‐invariant analysis of the fracture surface revealed three distinct zones with progressive increases in the Hurst exponent H (0.40 → 0.66) and in the characteristic scales l sc (0.2 → 1.9 μm) and L pz (11.5 → 27.4 μm), indicating increasingly correlated roughness during crack propagation. These findings demonstrate that quantitative fractography combined with scale‐invariant parameters can effectively capture the transition from short‐range, disorder‐dominated fracture initiation to long‐range, correlated crack growth in additively manufactured metals under very‐high‐cycle fatigue loading.

papers.title: From Large Language Models to Agentic Systems: A Systematic Review of Generative AI in GIScience
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly reshaping GIScience, yet the field has grown faster than its foundations have been systematically assessed. This review synthesizes how large language models (LLMs), vision‐language models (VLMs), diffusion models, and other generative approaches are deployed across geographic research. Screening an initial pool of 1146 records from the Web of Science, we identified 295 peer‐reviewed journal and conference papers published between November 2022 and February 2026 that demonstrate substantive engagement with geospatial analysis. Utilizing a 31‐variable extraction framework, this review combines corpus‐level descriptive statistics, thematic synthesis, and cross‐cutting evaluations of methodological trends, openness, trustworthiness, and geographic grounding. The literature reveals explosive growth, with LLMs remaining the dominant model family while multimodal pipelines and hybrid systems become increasingly prominent. However, our cross‐cutting synthesis exposes persistent structural gaps: formal uncertainty quantification remains rare; hallucination and geographic bias are unevenly addressed; full code‐and‐data openness is heavily limited; and explicit engagement with geographic theory remains incomplete, particularly within technically intensive areas like remote sensing and spatiotemporal modeling. Looking forward, we argue that disciplinary maturity depends on establishing five strategic pillars: geographically grounded uncertainty standards, spatial equity and justice frameworks, geospatially specific reproducibility norms, theory‐informed model design, and agentic GIS architectures that systematically transfer mature computer‐science mechanisms—including tool use, multi‐agent planning, reflection, persistent memory, and trajectory‐based evaluation—into spatially constrained, auditable geographic systems.

papers.abstract: Purpose. To systematize modern machine learning (ML) methods for the intelligent control of wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) and to identify priority directions for further research. Research methods. Critical analysis and synthesis of information from contemporary scientific publications; systematization of machine learning methods according to WAAM tasks – regression models (Random Forest, LightGBM, artificial neural networks), computer vision architectures (CNN, U-Net, YOLO), recurrent networks (LSTM), reinforcement learning methods, and physics-informed neural networks (PINN). Results. Modern ML methods for the intelligent control of WAAM have been systematized according to key technological tasks: predicting the geometric shape and dimensions of deposited beads, analysing the geometric dimensions of the weld pool using computer vision, and adaptive process control. The authors describe the web-based software (CAM system) they developed, which incorporates artificial intelligence, implements the full cycle from a 3D model to control code (G-code), and provides recommendations on deposition modes. Scientific novelty. A holistic systematization of machine learning methods for WAAM intelligent control is proposed, linking ML model types to specific technological tasks and outlining under-researched directions, in particular the application of physics-informed neural networks and digital twins for adaptive process control. Practical value. The developed software enables automation of WAAM process preparation – from 3D-model processing to G-code generation and deposition mode selection – improving the accuracy, reproducibility, and efficiency of additive manufacturing.

papers.title: Адитивне виробництво індивідуальних титанових імплантатів в ортопедії та травматології: сучасний стан, клінічне застосування та перспективи
papers.abstract: Background. The increasing number of revision orthopedic procedures, together with the prevalence of extensive post-traumatic, combat-related, and oncological bone defects, creates a growing need for new approaches to musculoskeletal reconstruction. Conventional implants may not adequately restore anatomy and biomechanics in patients with complex bone defects. Additive manufacturing enables the development of patient-specific titanium implants with tailored geometric, mechanical, and biological characteristics. Objective. To summarize current approaches to the design and additive manufacturing of patient-specific titanium implants in orthopedics and traumatology and to characterize their clinical applications, advantages, limitations, and future development prospects. Materials and Methods. A review of the scientific literature was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. The analysis primarily included publications from the last five years as well as fundamental studies addressing additive manufacturing of orthopedic implants. The clinical and engineering workflow of patient-specific implant development, manufacturing technologies, porous structure design, surface modification, and clinical applications were analyzed. Results. Additive manufacturing enables the development of patient-specific titanium implants based on computed tomography data, three-dimensional reconstruction, and CAD design. The use of Ti-6Al-4V ELI alloy and laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the manufacturing of complex geometries and the integration of controlled porous structures. Optimization of pore size, overall porosity, strut thickness, and lattice architecture promotes osseointegration, reduces stress shielding, and improves mechanical load distribution. Patient-specific implants have considerable clinical potential in revision arthroplasty, reconstruction of extensive post-traumatic and combat-related bone defects, orthopedic oncology, and the treatment of complex anatomical deformities. Major limitations include high manufacturing costs, the complexity and duration of the production workflow, and the limited number of prospective multicenter studies with long-term follow-up. Conclusions. Additive manufacturing of patient-specific titanium implants represents a promising approach in personalized reconstructive orthopedics and traumatology. The integration of digital planning, additive manufacturing, and optimized porous structures enables the development of implants adapted to the anatomical and functional requirements of individual patients. Further research should focus on long-term clinical outcomes, standardization of manufacturing workflows, and evaluation of the cost-effectiveness of widespread clinical implementation.

papers.title: Проєктування індивідуальних сітчастих титанових кейджів для реконструкції дефектів кісток після високоенергетичних травм
papers.abstract: High-energy musculoskeletal trauma may result in extensive bone loss and the formation of segmental long-bone defects. Reconstruction becomes particularly challenging in defects of the femur, tibia, humerus, radius and ulna, igh-energy injuries of the musculoskeletal system are frequently associated with comminuted fractures, extensive soft-tissue damage, and substantial loss of bone tissue, resulting in complex segmental defects of the long bones. Reconstruction of such defects, particularly in the femur, tibia, humerus, radius, and ulna, requires simultaneous restoration of anatomical length and alignment, mechanical stability, and conditions favorable for bone regeneration. Conventional reconstructive techniques, including autologous and allogeneic bone grafting, vascularized bone transfers, distraction osteogenesis, the induced membrane (Masquelet) technique, and segmental prosthetic reconstruction, may require multiple surgical procedures and prolonged rehabilitation. The development of computed tomography, three-dimensional modelling, computer-aided design, and additive manufacturing has enabled the creation of patient-specific titanium implants adapted to the individual geometry of a bone defect. This review analyzes current approaches to the design and clinical application of individual titanium mesh cages for reconstruction of large post-traumatic bone defects. Particular attention is given to the main stages of digital planning, including CT-based reconstruction, segmentation of bone structures, three-dimensional modelling, assessment of defect geometry, restoration of the anatomical axis and segment length, CAD-based cage design, and selection of fixation strategies. The structural characteristics of titanium mesh cages are also considered, including external geometry, porosity, pore size, strut thickness, and internal volume available for bone grafting. The combination of mechanical stabilization and biological support is one of the principal advantages of these implants. Their internal space can be filled with autologous or other bone-grafting materials, while the porous structure may facilitate bone ingrowth and osseointegration. Published clinical data indicate promising outcomes of patient-specific titanium cages in the reconstruction of segmental defects of the femur, tibia, and humerus, including cases treated in combination with internal fixation and the Masquelet technique. However, available evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, and the optimal design parameters cannot be considered universal. Further development should focus on individualized optimization of lattice geometry and porosity, mechanical and fatigue strength, fixation strategy, finite-element assessment of load distribution, and evaluation of long-term osseointegration. Patient-specific titanium mesh cages therefore represent a promising approach for restoring structural integrity and facilitating functional recovery after severe high-energy bone injuries.

papers.title: Benchmarking machine learning algorithms for high-fidelity power forecasting in utility-scale PV plants
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of photovoltaic (PV) power is essential for effective monitoring, control, and grid integration of large-scale solar systems. This study uses high-resolution data from a 20 MW utility-scale PV plant to benchmark four advanced machine learning (ML) models: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). Model performance was evaluated using R², RMSE, and MAE. Additionally, a thorough analysis of the three-dimensional (3D) predicted power surfaces was conducted. The findings indicate that GPR and ANN outperform SVM and RF, achieving near-perfect accuracy (R² = 1.0000) with minimal error. These methods yield smooth, physically consistent surfaces that accurately represent PV system behaviour. These findings establish GPR and ANN as the most reliable machine learning (ML) approaches for high-fidelity photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting and energy management applications.

papers.title: Impact Wear Performance Of Fdm-Printed Pla: Influence Of Infill Pattern And Density
papers.abstract: This study investigates the influence of infill pattern and infill density on the impact wear behavior of FDM-printed PLA specimens. Samples were manufactured using three internal architectures (cubic, gyroid, and triangular) at two infill densities (75% and 100%) and tested under cyclic impact loading conditions. Crater diameter, crater depth, and wear volume were quantified using three-dimensional optical profilometry.The results indicate that increasing the infill density significantly improved wear resistance by reducing crater dimensions and material loss. Among the investigated architectures, the triangular pattern exhibited the lowest wear volume (0.044 mm³) and the most stable crater morphology, indicating a more efficient load-transfer capability. Statistical analysis indicated that crater diameter was significantly affected by infill pattern and, in the two-way model, by infill density, whereas crater depth and wear volume showed non-significant but consistent trends.Contact mechanics analysis indicated that the calculated Hertzian contact pressures exceeded the yielding threshold of PLA, demonstrating that the wear process occurred in an elastic–plastic regime. Cross-sectional optical observations further revealed that damage evolution transitions from subsurface collapse in cubic structures to surface-confined deformation in triangular patterns. These findings highlight the critical role of internal architecture in determining the impact wear performance of additively manufactured polymer components.

papers.title: Motion Generalization in Humanoid Musculoskeletal Robotic Arm via Brain-inspired Motor Primitive Composition
papers.abstract: Humanoid musculoskeletal robots driven by McKibben muscles offer inherent compliance and safe physical interaction, making them ideal for human-centered environments. However, developing the capacity for learning and generalizing reaching movements to new spatial targets remains a complex mission due to the sophisticated coordination required between perception, decision-making, and control mechanisms. Inspired by the human motor system, we propose a brain-inspired framework for motion learning and generalization on a musculoskeletal robotic arm, integrating two key neural principles: motor primitive encoding and cerebellum-inspired predictive correction. We first learn reusable motor primitives from sparse demonstrations using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) optimized via iterative imitation learning. To generalize to novel targets, we propose a Cerebellum-Inspired Analytic Motor Primitive Composition (CAMPC) method that integrates a differentiable forward model and muscle-synergy-aware regularization to compute optimal blending weights. Experiments show that our CAMPC method reduces mean positioning error to 2.45 cm in simulation and generalizes to hardware using human demonstrations without any reinforcement learning, thereby avoiding hazardous online policy exploration on fragile pneumatic actuators. On the physical robot, CAMPC attains the lowest mean error of 3.03 cm, outperforming other baselines (paired t-tests, p<0.05). This demonstrates that our brain-inspired method enables humanoid musculoskeletal robots to generalize to untrained static reaching targets with high accuracy and data efficiency within a constrained desktop workspace.

papers.title: Additive Manufacturing Processes for Healthcare Applications: A Review of Smart and Data-Driven Manufacturing Approaches
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing has become a game changer in healthcare, allowing the production of complex, patient-specific medical devices, implants, and biomaterials that are hard to produce with more traditional manufacturing paths. The increasing interconnection of smart manufacturing principles, data-intensive approaches, and artificial intelligence (AI) has also increased the dependability, quality, and scalability of additive manufacturing for clinical use. To identify the opportunity of additive manufacturing processes in the context of healthcare, this paper presents an in-depth overview of the additive manufacturing methods that apply to medical applications, including powder bed fusion, extrusion of material, binder jetting, and directed energy-deposition methods, along with their potentials, constraints, and areas of application. It is stressed that smart and data-driven additive manufacturing can achieve quality control, process optimization, and regulatory traceability in real time through real-time sensing, machine learning, and digital twins. The review also addresses the concept of sustainable and recyclable manufacturing and explains how additive manufacturing can be used to facilitate material efficiency, remanufacturing, and lifecycle optimization of healthcare systems. The synthesis of the latest developments in process technologies, AI implementation, and digital manufacturing systems offers a systematic comprehension of the role of smart, sustainable, and data-driven additive manufacturing in the next-generation healthcare system and clinical production setting, as detailed in this work. It is further noticed that with the application of digital twin in additive manufacturing, it can significantly minimize both experimentation and error, reduce faults, and expedite the time frame between design and manufacturing.

papers.title: Microstructure-dependent balance between cyclic stability and elastocaloric response in as-built LPBF NiTi
papers.abstract: Cyclic degradation of laser powder bed-fused (LPBF) NiTi reflects the competition between reversible martensitic transformation and irreversible deformation, yet how coupled processing-induced microstructures regulate this competition remains unclear. Three coupled microstructural states were generated using hatch spacings of 90, 80 and 70 μm, while the other processing parameters were held constant. The resulting samples had comparable density, near-equiatomic bulk composition and similar martensite-start and austenite-finish temperatures, but differed in grain morphology, texture, B2-matrix orientation gradients, indexed B19′ fraction and representative dislocation configurations. At a nominal maximum strain of 8%, the samples produced with hatch spacings of 90, 80 and 70 μm accumulated permanent strains of 4.53%, 1.89% and 1.54%, respectively, after 10,000 cycles. Their first-cycle temperature changes were 11.31, 11.11 and 7.54 K. The 80 μm sample retained an absolute temperature change of 10.15 K after 10,000 cycles and yielded the highest estimated COPmat within the series at a nominal strain of 6%. The 70 μm sample showed the greatest normalized retention but a smaller absolute temperature response, consistent with restricted transformation activity. Post-cycling XRD patterns remained B2-dominated in all samples, with the 90 μm condition showing the largest change in the B2(110) peak profile. Idealized atomistic calculations indicated that moderate initial dislocation content promoted the initiation of transformed local structures, whereas excessive content restricted their subsequent growth. These results establish a microstructure-dependent balance between resistance to irreversible cyclic deformation and retained elastocaloric response in as-built LPBF NiTi. The 80 μm condition provided the most favorable combination within the investigated series.

papers.title: APPLICATION OF THE INTERNET OF THINGS (IOT) IN HYDRO-METEOROLOGICAL MONITORING NETWORKS: ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND CHALLENGES
papers.abstract: Climate change, the increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events, and pressures for sustainable development have created an urgent need to modernize meteorological and hydrological (MH) monitoring systems. Traditional monitoring networks in Vietnam and many developing countries still face limitations regarding station density, data transmission latency, scalability, and operational costs. The Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a breakthrough solution due to its capability to connect distributed sensors, enable real-time data processing, and integrate artificial intelligence. This paper investigates the application of IoT in MH monitoring networks, focusing on system architecture analysis, technical performance evaluation, and identification of implementation challenges within the context of implementing Resolution 57-NQ/TW of the Party Central Committee on breakthroughs in science and technology development, innovation, and national digital transformation. The study employs systematic literature review, network simulation (NS-3/MATLAB), and multi-criteria analysis (AHP-SWOT) based on empirical data from pilot stations in Vietnam. Results propose an optimized layered IoT architecture for MH monitoring, integrating multi-parameter sensors, LPWAN communication protocols (LoRaWAN/NB-IoT), edge computing, and cloud platforms supporting digital twin modeling. Performance evaluation demonstrates that the IoT system achieves average latency under 2.1 seconds, packet loss rate below 1.8%, 68% reduction in energy consumption compared to traditional GSM systems, and measurement accuracy meeting WMO standards. The study also identifies challenges related to protocol standardization, data security, remote area operation sustainability, inter-sectoral data sharing mechanisms, and digital workforce capacity. The paper concludes that integrating IoT into MH monitoring networks is not merely a technical upgrade but a strategic driver for implementing Resolution 57-NQ/TW, promoting digital transformation in the natural resources and environment sector, enhancing forecasting capacity, early warning systems, and climate change adaptation decision-making. Key policy, technical, and institutional recommendations are proposed to guide synchronized, secure, and sustainable implementation in Vietnam...

papers.title: Effects of Guided Inquiry on Students’ Motivation and Critical Thinking in Renewable Energy Physics
papers.abstract: This study examined differences in students’ learning motivation and critical thinking skills following Guided Inquiry learning in Renewable Energy physics. A quantitative quasi-experimental method with a Post-test Only Control Group Design was conducted at SMAN 1 Gondang Tulungagung. The participants were 69 Grade X students selected through purposive sampling, comprising 36 students in the experimental class (X-5) and 33 students in the control class (X-4). The study was conducted over five meetings from January 23 to February 29, 2024. The experimental class received Guided Inquiry learning, while the control class received Direct Instruction. Learning motivation was measured using a 25-item questionnaire, and critical thinking skills were assessed using five essay questions based on the respective study indicators. Cronbach’s alpha coefficients were 0.862 for motivation and 0.621 for critical thinking skills. The experimental group obtained higher mean scores for motivation (M = 88.64, SD = 9.708) and critical thinking (M = 87.50, SD = 7.020) than the control group (M = 82.30, SD = 7.768; M = 82.58, SD = 5.019). Independent-samples t-tests showed significant between-group differences in motivation, t(67) = 2.976, p = .004, Cohen’s d = 0.717, and critical thinking, t(67) = 3.324, p = .001, Cohen’s d = 0.801. MANOVA indicated a significant multivariate difference, Pillai’s Trace = .203, Wilks’ Lambda = .797, F(2,66) = 8.414, p < .001, partial η² = .203. Practically, Guided Inquiry can be implemented through Renewable Energy investigations involving questions, hypotheses, experiments, data analysis, and conclusions to support active learning and evidence-based reasoning.

papers.abstract: This study was motivated by the low level of students' mathematical conceptual understanding and the limited use of instructional materials that support active learning in statistics. The study aimed to develop an Electronic Student Worksheet (E-LKPD) based on the Student Teams Achievement Division (STAD) cooperative learning model assisted by Canva that meets the criteria of validity, practicality, and effectiveness. This research employed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model, which consists of the Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation stages. The research subjects consisted of two validators, one mathematics teacher, and 12 seventh-grade students of SMP Negeri 8 Kerinci. The research instruments included validation sheets, teacher and student practicality questionnaires, and a mathematical conceptual understanding test. The results showed that the developed E-LKPD achieved validity percentages of 82.14% for the material aspect, 78% for the media aspect, and 80% for the design aspect, all categorized as valid.The practicality test results reached 86.66% from the teacher and 93% from the students, indicating a very practical category. The effectiveness of the product was demonstrated by the conceptual understanding test, in which 10 out of 12 students achieved learning mastery, resulting in an effectiveness percentage of 83.33%. Therefore, the Canva-assisted E-LKPD based on the Student Teams Achievement Division (STAD) cooperative learning model is considered valid, practical, and effective for use as a digital instructional material in teaching statistics to seventh-grade junior high school students.

papers.title: Method for generating program control signals for the positioning of a vessel supporting auv operations
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of ensuring stable hydroacoustic communication between an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) and support vessel or unmanned surface vessel (USV) supporting its operation during the AUV’s underwater missions in open sea conditions using an ultra-short baseline hydroacoustic communication and navigation system. Existing approaches to positioning the vessel relative to an AUV moving along an arbitrary route often lead to degradation or loss of communication due to increasing distance to the vehicle and growing vessel self-noise. To solve this problem, a method for generating program control signals for vessel positioning based on model predictive control is proposed. This method computes the vessel’s speed and yaw into account the actual and predicted AUV trajectories, the vessel’s dynamic characteristics, and the physical parameters of the hydroacoustic communication channel. In order to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), which accounts for signal propagation loss, vessel self-noise level, and sea ambient noise, an optimization objective function is formulated. The vessel’s state vector is predicted using its dynamic model incorporating the Nomoto yaw equation. The optimization problem is solved at each computation step by means of quadratic programming in the MATLAB environment. Numerical simulations were performed for an AUV trajectory consisting of successive tacks. Comparison with two alternative approaches demonstrated that the developed method ensures a consistently high SNR level, absence of communication loss, and minimal necessary vessel movements. The research findings confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed method for maintaining a reliable hydroacoustic communication channel with an AUV operating over extended sea areas.

papers.title: AI-powered PLE in an active learning strategy for teacher training
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to design, implement, and analyze a project-based learning strategy for teacher training within a personal learning environment mediated by artificial intelligence. Based on Educational Action Research, the study consisted of four phases: a) inquirydiagnosis; b) plan formulation; c) implementation and evaluation of results; d) feedback and analysis. The participants were faculty members at a public university on the Oaxacan coast of Mexico, who developed digital portfolios through Project-Based Learning. The findings show that faculty encourage deeper reflection to continually question the why, the purpose, and the how of integrating AI into the classroom. Analytical and critical thinking should not be replaced through the use of this technology. There are barriers to access, such as connectivity, the cost of platforms, and the availability of equipment. In conclusion, teacher training on AI competencies, when conducted within the PLE, promotes experiences in open spaces, with certain levels of autonomy, flexibility, and collaboration. Teachers have the opportunity to identify their preferences and teaching-learning strategies within the context of situated and meaningful education

papers.title: Next-Generation Cyber-Physical Systems: Architectures, Intelligent Technologies, Applications, and Future Research Directions
papers.abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) have evolved from tightly coupled sensing, computation, communication, and control platforms into highly distributed intelligent ecosystems in which physical processes, computational resources, communication infrastructures, artificial intelligence, digital twins, and human participants interact continuously. The emergence of edge and fog computing, 5G/6G networks, machine learning, reinforcement learning, federated learning, blockchain, digital twins, autonomous systems, and foundation models is substantially changing the architecture and operational characteristics of next-generation CPSs. Unlike conventional CPS architectures, emerging systems must simultaneously address real-time constraints, heterogeneous data, dynamic environments, distributed intelligence, safety, cybersecurity, privacy, explainability, interoperability, and lifecycle assurance. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of next-generation CPSs from architectural, technological, methodological, application, and research perspectives. A unified taxonomy is developed covering physical, sensing, communication, edge, cloud, intelligence, digital-twin, orchestration, security, and human-interaction layers. The review critically examines centralized, edge-centric, cloud-assisted, distributed, digital-twin-enabled, and AI-native architectures and compares their characteristics with respect to latency, scalability, resilience, computational requirements, interoperability, privacy, and assurance. Mathematical formulations are presented for CPS state estimation, control, resource optimization, anomaly detection, and multi-objective performance assessment. Emerging intelligent methodologies—including deep learning, reinforcement learning, federated learning, graph neural networks, physics-informed learning, generative AI, and foundation models—are analyzed in terms of their applicability and limitations. Applications in smart manufacturing, autonomous transportation, smart grids, healthcare, agriculture, buildings, robotics, and smart cities are discussed, followed by an illustrative industrial CPS case study integrating edge intelligence, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and secure control. Particular attention is given to benchmark datasets, simulation platforms, communication technologies, digital-twin frameworks, and cybersecurity mechanisms. Finally, unresolved challenges concerning real-time AI assurance, semantic interoperability, adversarial robustness, uncertainty quantification, energy efficiency, human autonomy, ethical governance, and verification of learning-enabled controllers are identified. The review concludes by proposing a research agenda toward trustworthy, adaptive, interoperable, and self-evolving CPS ecosystems.

papers.abstract: This study was motivated by the low level of mathematical problem-solving skills among elementary school students and the limited use of active learning models and instructional media. This quantitative research employed a quasi-experimental method with a nonequivalent control group design to examine the effect of the Problem-Based Learning model assisted by Modified Congklak media on the mathematical problem-solving skills of fourth-grade students at SDN 1 Nagri Kidul. The sample consisted of 54 students divided into an experimental group and a control group. Data were collected through pretests and posttests and then analyzed using prerequisite tests and simple linear regression analysis. The results indicated that the data were normally distributed and homogeneous. The Problem-Based Learning model assisted by Modified Congklak media made a significant contribution of 55.4% to the improvement of students’ mathematical problem-solving skills. It can be concluded that this model is an effective alternative strategy for mathematics instruction in elementary schools.

papers.abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of scientific publications on proactive teaching and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in education published between 2020 and 2025. The aim of the study is to identify key trends, research priorities, and the characteristics of the development of the research community in this field. The empirical basis of the study consists of Scopus data processed using Elsevier's SciVal analytical platform. The results reveal a consistent rise in publishing efforts, especially from 2023 onward, suggesting an increasing enthusiasm for the active teaching method amid the digital evolution of education. The Asia-Pacific region, particularly China, holds leading positions in terms of publication output and scientific impact. Among the most productive and highly cited researchers, Gašević Dragan stands out. The findings contribute to a better understanding of the transformation of teachers' professional roles in the context of digitalization and provide a foundation for further interdisciplinary research. The scientific novelty of the study lies in identifying the degree of thematic integration between research on proactive teaching behavior and artificial intelligence in education based on a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed publications from 2020 to 2025. Unlike studies that examine AI primarily from technological or didactic perspectives, the present research assesses the representation of professional proactivity and teacher agency within the emerging interdisciplinary research landscape. The examination of the material demonstrated the prevalence of research fields like active learning, metacognition, students' viewpoints, educator training, post-secondary education, and generative AI. The results can be utilized in subsequent theoretical and empirical investigations, in addition to shaping educational approaches and professional growth initiatives for instructors designed to promote active engagement and the successful incorporation of AI tools in teaching practices.

papers.title: Effects of on-site mechano-bioengineering process on alginate bioink printing for bone tissue engineering using Biowork Pen® and gelatin-encapsulated octacalcium phosphate particles: An in vitro and in vivo study
papers.abstract: On-site mechano-bioengineering of bioink within a handheld biopen barrel holds significant potential for enhancing both mechanical and biological properties in bioprinting applications. The process dynamically micro-controls component behaviors during continuous extrusion. In this study, we addressed the ‘black box’ behaviors of passive bioink in a syringe extrusion printing using an on-site mechano-bioengineering approach. Utilizing our novel twin-screw Biowork Pen®, we proved that controlled bioink engineering of cell distribution and mechano-stimulation significantly enhances bioactivity. The bioactive properties of octacalcium phosphate (OCP) particles are improved by gelatin encapsulation for its better cell supportiveness. Alginate bioink containing cells and gelatin-encapsulated OCP (OCP-G) particles was mechano-engineered within the biomixing barrel of Biowork Pen® to optimize its physical, biological, and printing properties. This on-site bioengineering process ensured homogeneity in distribution of cells and OCP particles within the alginate gel network under controlled shear flow. OCP particles with 1.5 wt% gelatin exhibited 35% smaller diameter than unmodified OCP, suggesting that dense entrapment of OCP by gelatin hindered crystal growth during synthesis. In vitro tests demonstrated enhanced cell viability and accelerated growth rates (up to 40%/day) for the OCP-G samples, outperforming both alginate (29%/day) and unmodified OCP-alginate (25%/day) gels. Furthermore, glycosaminoglycan (up to 1.9 mg/ml), collagen (up to 80 mg/ml), and alkaline phosphatase (up to 130%) secretions were markedly higher in the OCP-G bioinks. In vivo evaluations indicated that this integrated bioink engineering and extrusion approach reduced inflammatory responses (CD68) and promoted robust tissue infiltration within the implant. Overall, the mechano-bioengineering of OCP-G bioinks with the novel Biowork Pen® significantly improves both biological and mechanical performance, offering promising advancements in functional tissue engineering.

papers.title: An Idea to Explore: AI ‐Supported Digital Twin Laboratory for Risk‐Reduced and Immersive Biochemistry Education
papers.abstract: Biochemistry education faces persistent challenges in equipping students with the skills required to manage complex laboratory protocols, advanced instrumentation, and analytical procedures, particularly in high-risk or resource-intensive experimental settings. Traditional hands-on training is constrained by limited access to equipment, safety concerns, and high operational costs, hindering institutions from providing realistic and scalable laboratory experiences. However, Digital Twin technology presents a transformative alternative. It creates simulations of real biochemical laboratories, providing immersive, scalable, and cost-efficient environments unconstrained by physical limitations. This approach supports interactive, avatar-mediated engagement that bridges conceptual knowledge with applied practice. In this study, we aimed to introduce BioDTLab, a custom Digital Twin framework for biochemistry education that integrates Virtual Reality, Internet of Things, robotics, data analytics, and an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven Virtual Chat-GPT Tutor. BioDTLab synchronizes physical and digital domains to provide high-fidelity simulations of biochemical processes and instrumentation, while the AI-driven Virtual Chat-GPT Tutor evaluates student engagement, comprehension, and procedural accuracy. Our findings demonstrate that Digital Twin frameworks, such as BioDTLab, can redefine biochemistry education by making advanced experiential learning more accessible, safe, and scalable, while reducing reliance on costly physical resources. BioDTLab integrates immersive simulation, real-time data synchronization, and AI-driven feedback to provide a sustainable model for future science education that enhances conceptual understanding and practical competence. In addition, its adaptability makes it suitable for instructional models, such as the flipped classroom, where pre-laboratory virtual practice can complement and enhance in-person laboratory training.

papers.title: Hybrid PID-reinforcement learning control for active vibration suppression in milling processes
papers.abstract: Abstract This study examines a PID baseline augmented by a bounded soft actor-critic (SAC) residual and a Lyapunov-inspired action filter for active vibration suppression in milling. A two-axis nonlinear regenerative model and equivalent active vibration damper define the simulation framework. The research question concerns the incremental value and actuation cost of residual learning relative to conventional feedback, rather than the novelty of combining PID and reinforcement learning. The retained numerical summaries report competitive nominal attenuation and lower aggregate vibration under parameter variation at greater RMS actuation effort. These summaries are considered descriptive reports of the integrated controller, not independently verified evidence that learning or filtering causes the reported differences. The theoretical analysis establishes conditional ultimate boundedness of a reduced PID error model under nominal Hurwitz stability and an independently justified additive-perturbation bound. It does not certify the complete regenerative-delay system, physical machine safety or SAC optimality. Model-parameter sensitivity is distinguished from generalization to unseen machining conditions, and mathematical boundedness is distinguished from chatter stability. Matched component ablations, traceable training and test records, and independent model validation remain necessary to substantiate the numerical claims and establish a manufacturing benefit. The contribution is therefore a constrained residual-control formulation and a qualified assessment of its reported vibration–actuation trade-off.

papers.title: Large language model-driven inverse design of acoustic valley-Hall insulators
papers.abstract: Abstract Acoustic valley-Hall insulators (AVHIs) are an emerging class of acoustic topological materials that enable robust directional wave transport and show promise for applications in communication, sensing and wave manipulation. This study presents a large language model (LLM)-driven inverse design framework consisting of two collaborative agents. The Designer-LLM is fine-tuned on an AVHI database generated through reinforcement learning to perform bandgap-targeted inverse design. The Manager-LLM coordinates task planning, semantic parsing, simulation tool invocation and multimodal result generation. With this framework, multimodal design outputs, including structural parameters, band structures, eigenmode fields, and manufacturable model files, can be generated according to concise design requirements. Bandgap error analysis on test sets indicates that the fine-tuned Designer-LLM generates AVHI structures with reliable bandgap-matching accuracy. Overall, this study proposes a modular LLM-agent framework for the inverse design of AVHIs. The framework integrates semantic interaction, AVHI inverse design, numerical verification, and multimodal result generation into a unified workflow and can provide a useful reference for future extensions to other acoustic metamaterial design tasks.

papers.title: Boosting Chiral Separation Through Sinuous 3D Nanochannels With Saddle–Splay Curvature in Biomimetic Membranes
papers.abstract: Biological systems commonly leverage curved and geometrically complex transport pathways to create pockets and constrictions for precise molecular discrimination. In contrast, synthetic separation membranes mainly achieve selectivity through controlled pore size and surface chemistry, facing challenges in separating molecules that differ subtly in shape or stereochemistry. Here we report self-assembled polymeric membranes with sinuous 3D nanochannels whose intrinsic saddle-splay geometry boosts chiral separation. Freestanding nanoporous membranes are readily fabricated by photocuring lyotropic double-gyroid (GYR) liquid crystals (LCs) formed from amphiphiles bearing chiral moieties. Spatial variation in saddle-splay curvature within these GYR nanochannels clusters chiral selectors into precisely positioned "checkpoints" and imposes strong nanoconfinement, forcing racemates to repeatedly traverse these unavoidable stereoselective sites that cumulatively amplify enantioselectivity. The highly permeable membranes achieve enantiopure separation of model racemates such as ibuprofen, with selectivity nearly 10-fold higher than their counterparts with sheet-like or cylindrical-mesh pores of comparable chemistry and size. This work establishes sinuous 3D nanochannels with saddle-splay curvature as a biomimetic structural motif for amplifying chiral recognition in synthetic membranes.

papers.title: Intelligent security policy generation algorithm based on graph neural network and reinforcement learning for SD-WAN
papers.abstract: With the evolution of enterprise networks to multi-site and cloud architectures, Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) is prone to the problems of insufficient global policy regulation and frequent policy adjustment under dynamic security threats, which in turn leads to increased delay, aggravated packet loss and unstable network operation. Existing research mostly focuses on traffic optimization or local security detection, lacking global topology security situation modeling for SD-WAN and intelligent policy generation mechanisms that balance security benefits and policy stability. To address these issues, this study proposes an intelligent security policy generation model for dynamic security threats, Security-aware Graph-based Dual Reinforcement Learning for SD-WAN (SGDRL-SDWAN). The study achieves joint representation of network topology and security risks through constructing a security-aware graph neural network. Additionally, it designs a two-stage reinforcement learning framework with collaborative optimization of policy generation and stability constraints, realizing adaptive generation and stable control of security policies. The simulation environment is built based on open network traffic and intrusion detection data for verification. The experimental results show that SGDRL-SDWAN can reduce the end-to-end delay to 52.34 ms and the packet loss rate to 0.82% in the dynamic attack scenario, and effectively alleviate the problem of link load concentration. Under the conditions of persistent attacks and load fluctuation, the number of policy updates and network performance jitter are significantly lower than those of the comparison model. This study aims to provide a deployable intelligent security policy generation method for enterprise network operators and SD-WAN management platforms. It supports automatic generation and continuous optimization of security policies in dynamic attack environments, reducing control oscillations and operational burdens caused by manual policy adjustments, thereby enhancing network security and operational stability while lowering operational complexity.

papers.title: Adaptive Fuzzy LMS Control for Positioning and Anti-Sway of an Overhead Crane System
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper formulates an adaptive fuzzy control approach for the overhead crane positioning and anti-sway problem. The crane is treated as an underactuated nonlinear system with four states, one horizontal force input, and two controlled outputs: trolley position and load swing angle. The introductory part of the paper is extended with a crane control-oriented literature overview that distinguishes open-loop input shaping and command smoothing, model-based feedback control, fuzzy and LMI-based control, data-driven and model-free adaptive control, reinforcement learning, and machine learning-based approaches. The control design is then developed from a compact Takagi–Sugeno fuzzy state-space representation of the nonlinear cart–pendulum crane dynamics. The fuzzy model is obtained by sector nonlinearity and local approximation in fuzzy partition spaces, resulting in two local rules scheduled by the load swing angle. A parallel distributed fuzzy controller is parameterized as a linear-in-the-parameters control law, and its local parameters are adapted online by a teacher-based normalized least mean squares (LMS) rule. The adaptive controller learns the control signal of a virtual supervisory fuzzy controller and then remains active as the controller in the test phase. Projection, leakage regularization, force saturation, and a smooth transfer from the supervisory signal to the learned LMS signal are included to obtain an implementation-oriented closed-loop formulation. The proposed approach is intended as a physically interpretable bridge between robust fuzzy crane modeling and data-driven adaptive control. The novelty is clarified as the integration of a compact fuzzy crane model, a supervisory teacher signal, normalized LMS learning, leakage/projection, input saturation, and command-governed anti-sway tuning in one simulation-oriented framework. The study is explicitly presented as a numerical benchmark; formal nonlinear stability certification and laboratory validation are identified as future work rather than as claims of the present contribution.

papers.title: Machine learning for thermal energy storage in buildings: A Physics-first systematic review of sensible, latent and sorption storage
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is widely used for reduced-order modeling, prediction and control of thermal energy storage (TES) in buildings, yet the field lacks a critical synthesis linking modeling choices to storage physics. The objective of this review is to establish, quantitatively, how ML is actually used for building-scale TES and where practice diverges from the physics of the storage process. Its novelty is twofold: it is the first review to organize the TES–ML literature by storage mechanism rather than by algorithm or task, and the first to perform a cross-study quantitative synthesis of architectures, metrics and validation practice. This review critically analyzes 40 peer-reviewed studies published between 1999 and 2025, identified through a systematic, PRISMA 2020-style screening (last search update: December 2025), using a physics-first taxonomy organized by storage mechanism, i.e. sensible, latent and sorption/thermochemical, rather than by algorithm or material. Sensible and latent storage dominate (about 42% and 48% of studies); sorption and thermochemical storage remain underrepresented (about 10%). Of 38 catalogued models, 25 (66%) belong to the feedforward/multilayer-perceptron family, 10 are recurrent (RNN, LSTM, GRU, NARX), 2 use deep reinforcement learning and only 1 is physics-informed; of the 27 architectures whose depth is explicitly reported, all but two use three or fewer hidden layers. Where reported, models reproduce reference data accurately with correlation coefficients frequently above 0.99 and, in one surrogate, a speed-up from roughly 120 h to 5 s. However, performance is communicated through at least seven different metric conventions (R/R², RMSE, CVRMSE, MSE, MAE, relative error and system-level savings), only four studies report a model-fidelity metric together with a system-level outcome, and validation, dataset construction and computational baselines are reported too heterogeneously for direct comparison. The central research gap is a mismatch between the inherently transient physics of TES and the static quantities most models predict; recurrent, hybrid and physics-informed approaches that could close it remain sparsely validated. We translate these findings into a prioritized research agenda: shared benchmark problems, open datasets, a minimum reporting checklist for TES-ML studies, and an explicit mapping from storage mechanism to suitable model family.

papers.title: The Avian Digital Twin Intelligence: A Multimodal AI, Bioacoustic and Precision- Phenotyping Framework for Predictive Health, Disease Forecasting and Welfare Optimization in Companion Parrots
papers.abstract: Companion parrots present an unusually complex challenge for preventive veterinary medicine because clinically meaningful changes may initially manifest as subtle alterations in behaviour, vocal activity, posture, locomotion, feeding, social interaction, plumage condition or daily activity patterns. Conventional clinical assessment generally provides a snapshot of an animal at a particular point in time, whereas companion parrots continuously generate behavioural and environmental information that could potentially be transformed into longitudinal health indicators. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), multimodal sensing, computer vision, bioacoustics, self-supervised learning and time-series modelling create an opportunity to develop a fundamentally different paradigm: the individualized avian digital twin.An avian digital twin can be conceptualized as a continuously updated computational representation of an individual bird that integrates heterogeneous observations—including video, vocalizations, activity, environmental conditions, feeding behaviour, physiological measurements and veterinary records—with biological and statistical models. Rather than relying exclusively on population-level thresholds, such a system could establish an individualized baseline and detect deviations in multimodal trajectories. Computer vision could quantify posture, locomotion, plumage appearance and activity; bioacoustic models could characterize vocal repertoire, temporal structure and acoustic features; environmental sensors could contextualize behavioural changes; and longitudinal machine-learning models could integrate these signals into probabilistic health and welfare trajectories.This framework is particularly relevant to parrots because vocal learning, social complexity and individual behavioural variation make simplistic interpretation of single behavioural signals problematic. Recent literature also demonstrates both the promise and the limitations of automated animal bioacoustics and AI-based welfare monitoring. Importantly, a 2024 systematic review identified substantial gaps in validated parrot-specific welfare indicators, while a 2026 expert-developed tool, PsittaWel, provides a structured framework encompassing physical health, activity, enrichment, nutrition, social behaviour, human–animal interactions and maladaptive behaviours. This article proposes a Multimodal Avian Intelligence Architecture (MAIA) integrating individual digital twins, foundation-model representations, explainable AI, uncertainty quantification, causal inference, federated learning and edge computing. The objective is not to replace veterinary diagnosis but to establish a continuous decision-support layer capable of identifying clinically relevant deviations earlier, prioritizing veterinary assessment and supporting individualized welfare optimization. Major challenges include dataset scarcity, species and individual variability, annotation quality, confounding environmental factors, algorithmic bias, interpretability, validation, privacy and the risk of overinterpreting behavioural correlates as disease-specific biomarkers. A clinically credible avian digital twin therefore requires prospective validation against veterinary ground truth, calibrated uncertainty and human oversight.Keywords: companion parrots; avian medicine; digital twin; artificial intelligence; multimodal AI; bioacoustics; computer vision; precision veterinary medicine; animal welfare; digital phenotyping; foundation models; explainable AI; uncertainty quantification; predictive health.
