papers.title: СУЧАСНІ ПІДХОДИ ДО ОПТИМІЗАЦІЇ РЕАБІЛІТАЦІЇ ПАЦІЄНТІВ ПІСЛЯ ЕНДОПРОТЕЗУВАННЯ КУЛЬШОВОГО СУГЛОБА НА ГОСТРОМУ ТА ПІСЛЯГОСТРОМУ ЕТАПАХ
papers.abstract: The article presents a review-based analytical synthesis of modern approaches to optimizing rehabilitation after total hip arthroplasty during the acute and post-acute stages. The relevance of the topic is determined by the fact that surgical elimination of pain and restoration of anatomical support do not automatically ensure complete functional recovery, because postoperative mobility depends on muscle reserve, postural control, fall risk, cognitive ability to follow instructions, adherence to exercise, comorbidity profile and access to rehabilitation support. The aim of the study was to compare enhanced recovery pathways, early mobilization, weight bearing as tolerated, home-based exercise programs, supervised physical therapy, telerehabilitation, virtual reality, progressive resistance training, balance and gait training, aquatic exercise and activity liberalization in terms of effectiveness, safety, clinical indications and further development prospects. The subject of this study is approaches to the rehabilitation of patients following joint replacement surgery. The study was designed as a narrative review with elements of a systematized search of publications from 2021 to 2026 in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library and Google Scholar. Hip replacement surgery helps eliminate chronic pain, restore weight-bearing function to the limb, and significantly improve the quality of life for patients with end-stage degenerative, post-traumatic, or necrotic hip joint conditions. The analysis showed that ERAS is the most justified framework for the acute stage, as it creates physiological and organizational prerequisites for early mobilization through multimodal analgesia, complication prevention, patient education and coordinated multidisciplinary care. During the post-acute stage, a structured home program is appropriate for low-risk patients with adequate self-management, telerehabilitation is preferable when regular feedback and adherence support are required, whereas supervised physical therapy is clinically prioritized in patients with gait instability, abductor weakness, fear of falling, cognitive barriers, poor technique or delayed functional progress. The review emphasizes that virtual reality, aquatic exercise, balance training and progressive resistance training should not be interpreted as interchangeable technologies, because each intervention targets a different mechanism of recovery and has a specific indication profile. The most promising direction is a personalized hybrid rehabilitation pathway that combines pre-discharge risk stratification, a minimum set of functional outcomes, remote monitoring, selective face-to-face supervision and technology-assisted modules matched to the patient’s dominant functional deficit. Optimizing rehabilitation after hip replacement should be based on a phased approach and risk stratification. In the acute phase, the most evidence-based approach is the ERAS protocol with early mobilization. It creates the physiological and organizational conditions for safe movement, rather than simply increasing the number of exercises.

papers.title: КРЕДИТНО-МОДУЛЬНА СИСТЕМА У НАВЧАЛЬНОМУ ПРОЦЕСІ СТУДЕНТІВ СПЕЦІАЛЬНОСТІ «ТЕРАПІЯ ТА РЕАБІЛІТАЦІЯ»
papers.abstract: In the current reality of russia’s full-scale military aggression against Ukraine, there has been a significant increase in demand among medical professionals for specialists with a bachelor’s degree in education in “Therapy and Rehabilitation”. Accordingly, the requirements for training such medical professionals have increased. A medical worker at this level is not just a “simple assistant” but, in essence, a partner to the doctor, performing many independent functions. The European Credit Transfer System (ECTS) provides a solid foundation for training such specialists, ensuring the acquisition of sufficient knowledge and mastery of relevant competencies. Our study aimed to identify and analyse opinions of students studying the speciality “Therapy and Rehabilitation” and academic staff of the Physiology department at IFNMU, their attitudes, and proposals regarding practical implementation and ways to improve the ECTS. We conducted an anonymous survey using questionnaires. Separate questionnaires were prepared for students and teachers, which included questions about their attitudes toward teaching academic disciplines in accordance with ECTS principles, the positive and negative aspects of the system, suggestions, and recommendations for improving and refining it. In total, the questionnaires contained 8 questions for teachers and 16 for students. Analysis of survey results suggests that not all students in the Faculty of Health Sciences at IFNMU are currently sufficiently prepared for ECTS-based learning and transition from passive to active learning, where independent and creative work is preferred. In fact, one of the key problems with the credit transfer system of education is that students are not fully focused on the priority of independent mastery of material in educational programmes and on significant extracurricular learning that accompanies it. Numerous students are clearly not well-adapted to higher education and lack significant internal motivation. The attitude towards the assessment system in general and test control in particular, as an integral part of the educational process and a method for controlling students’ knowledge, is ambiguous. Among the positive aspects of ECTS learning, the following are most often noted: the structured nature of academic discipline into modules and an objective assessment system, continuous and diverse preparation for classes, and sufficient mastery of practical skills and knowledge. It is important to note the following: most of teaching staff believe that insufficient funding and departments’ existing material and technical base limit possibility of fully utilising the credit-modular system of education. Conclusions based on the analysis of obtained results: a) at present time, there is an obvious ambiguity in the perception of ECTS by students of the Faculty of Health Sciences of IFNMU, who are studying in “Therapy and Rehabilitation” speciality, their readiness and attitude towards it with corresponding positive and negative aspects; b) it is necessary to continue working on the improvement and meaningful implementation of credit-modular system in order to maximise cooperation and create a closer relationship with the student audience; c) on the one hand, it is necessary to preserve maximally the positive achievements of the national education system, and on the other hand, to effectively use the existing experience of leading European countries.

papers.abstract: Providing foundational marketing knowledge is essential for preparing students for higher education. However, students differ in their prior knowledge and personal characteristics, which may affect their academic achievement. This research aimed to compare the learning achievement of undergraduate students in a basic marketing knowledge foundation program based on their personal characteristics. This study employed a quantitative research approach. The population consisted of 95 undergraduate students enrolled in the Bachelor of Business Administration Program in Marketing, Faculty of Management Sciences, Songkhla Rajabhat University, who participated in the basic marketing knowledge foundation program during the 2026 academic year. The research instruments included a personal information questionnaire and a learning achievement test. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including frequency and percentage, while inferential statistics consisted of the Independent Samples t-test and One-way Analysis of Variance (One-way ANOVA) The findings revealed that the majority of the respondents were male and resided in Songkhla Province. Furthermore, differences in personal characteristics, including gender, domicile, type of educational institution from which the students had previously graduated, and previous cumulative grade point average (GPA), did not result in statistically significant differences in learning achievement in the basic marketing knowledge foundation program at the .05 level. The findings reflect that the implementation of a foundational learning program integrating lectures with active learning, in which students actively participated in constructing knowledge through hands-on activities and collaborative learning, while engaging in activities involving critical thinking, problem analysis, collaborative problem-solving, and classroom presentations, could reduce differences in students’ prior knowledge and promote equal readiness for further study in marketing-related courses

papers.abstract: This research aimed to:(1) examine the current conditions, desirable conditions, and priority needs for strategic leadership among school administrators in promoting teachers’ active learning instruction; (2) develop a strategic leadership model for school administrators to enhance teachers’ active learning instruction; and (3) evaluate the validity, appropriateness, feasibility, and usefulness of the developed model. A mixed-methods research design was employed. The participants and key informants consisted of 30 school administrators and teachers selected through purposive sampling. The research instruments included: (1) a questionnaire assessing current conditions, desirable conditions, and priority needs; (2) focus group discussions and in-depth interviews; and (3) an expert evaluation form used to assess the quality of the proposed model. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including mean and standard deviation, as well as the Priority Needs Index (PNI), while qualitative data were analyzed through content analysis. The findings indicated that: 1.The current level of strategic management and overall educational quality was moderate, whereas the desirable level was rated at the highest level; 2.The EPCED Strategic Leadership Model was developed, comprising three core dimensions: strategic thinking, change leadership, and collaborative management; 3.The model demonstrated the highest levels of validity, appropriateness, feasibility, and usefulness. The model integrates priority needs assessment and problem analysis, particularly in the domain of change management, with the effective utilization of instructional media and learning resources. Therefore, it provides a systematic and practical framework for school administrators to strengthen teachers’ active learning instruction and improve educational quality effectively.

papers.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of the principal's academic supervision on the pedagogical competence of teachers in public junior high schools in North Padang District. Teacher pedagogical competence is an ability that must be possessed by a teacher, but some teachers experience problems characterized by teachers who have difficulty in adapting learning methods to student learning styles, creating an active learning atmosphere, and lacking in utilizing learning technology. One factor suspected to be an influence on these problems is the principal's academic supervision which includes the implementation of supervision, the tools used during supervision, and the results of follow-up supervision. This study uses a quantitative approach with a correlational research type. The study population comprised all teachers at public junior high schools in North Padang District, with a sample of 103 teachers selected using proportional stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a questionnaire that had been tested for validity and reliability. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics and simple linear regression. The results showed that the principal's academic supervision was in the very good category, while the teachers' pedagogical competence was also in the very good category. The regression test results indicated that the principal's supervision significantly influenced the teachers' pedagogical competence. This finding indicates that the better the quality of academic supervision, the better the teachers' pedagogical competence. Therefore, teachers need to improve their pedagogical competence, especially in the teaching and learning process in the classroom. Because learning implementation is a key to success in improving student learning outcomes, supervision should be conducted weekly for teachers, and supervisors should provide regular training to improve teachers' pedagogical competence.

Operational definitions and indicators were then developed and evaluated for appropriateness by seven experts. In Phase 2, the model was tested using data collected from 500 school administrators and teachers selected through multistage random sampling. The research instrument was a five-point rating scale questionnaire. The item-objective congruence indices ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, the discrimination indices ranged from 0.271 to 0.725, and the reliability coefficient was 0.946. The data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis. In Phase 3, a manual for using the indicators was developed and evaluated for appropriateness by five experts. papers.abstract: This research article aims to investigate the current conditions and problems regarding the management of English communication instruction for pre - service teachers in higher education institutions in the lower southern region. The sample used in this study consisted of 123 second - year student teachers majoring in English, who were selected through stratified random sampling proportional to the size of each institution. The research instruments for data collection included questionnaires, in - depth interviews, and focus group discussions. The statistics used for data analysis were percentages, means, standard deviation, and content analysis. The research findings revealed that, overall, the students' opinions on the problems regarding English communication were at a moderate level ( = 3.25, S.D. = 0.86). The most significant issues were anxiety over grammatical accuracy, which consequently deterred them from communicating fluently ( = 3.61, S.D. = 0.94), and the difficulty in selecting vocabulary appropriate for the context of the teaching profession ( = 3.61, S.D. = 0.97). Regarding the current conditions and phonetic problems, the students indicated that the influence of their native dialect's phonological structure directly affected their English pronunciation and stress patterns ( = 3.10, S.D. = 0.88). In terms of the needs for instructional management, overall needs were at a high level ( = 4.19, S.D. = 0.85), with the highest level of need expressed for instructors to help create a learning atmosphere that reduces anxiety ( = 4.70, S.D. = 0.67), provide support and guidance during activities ( = 4.50, S.D. = 0.71), and act as facilitators in organizing highly effective active learning activities rather than relying solely on conventional lectures.

papers.abstract: The objectives of this research article were: 1) to study the state of digital learning management of the Thakhanun–Sahakon Nikhom Educational Management Network School Group, Kanchanaburi Province; 2) to study the methods for digital learning management based on the Five Bāhussuta Principles; and 3) to propose guidelines for digital learning management based on the Five Bāhussuta Principles for the network schools. This study employed a mixed-methods approach. The quantitative component utilized questionnaires administered to the entire population of 153 participants, with data analyzed using percentages, means, and standard deviations. The qualitative component involved interviews with 7 key informants, and the data were analyzed using content analysis. The research findings revealed that: 1) The state of digital learning management of the network schools was overall at a high level. Ranking from highest to lowest mean scores, the aspects were: Digital Communication, followed by Digital Access, Digital Media Analysis, Digital Media Creation, and Digital Media Usage, respectively. 2) The methods for digital learning management based on the Five Bāhussuta Principles included: Digital Media Creation, emphasizing context-based design with teachers acting as innovators who integrate knowledge; Digital Media Usage, focusing on Active Learning through Learning Management Systems (LMS) under teacher guidance; Digital Access, collaborating to allocate devices, reduce inequality, and provide equal opportunities; Digital Communication, utilizing communication platforms to build Professional Learning Communities (PLC) and accelerate teacher capacity development; and Digital Media Analysis, fostering critical judgment to filter information and utilizing Big Data for comprehensive analysis. 3) The guidelines for digital learning management based on the Five Bāhussuta Principles were: Digital Media Creation involves comprehensive data collection, summarizing key points for easy retention, emphasizing interactivity, stimulating deep critical thinking, and applying technology to create tangible works. Digital Media Usage employs wisdom to access and verify information, transferring knowledge for review, reflecting on the essence, and analytically linking theory to correct practice. Digital Access requires openness to diverse information, accurate recall key points, exchanging opinions, considering thoroughly to achieve mastery, and distinguishing facts to synthesize personal insights. Digital Communication requires mindfulness in filtering information before sharing, communicating with polite language appropriate to the time, place, and target audience to maximize benefits through mutual understanding. Digital Media Analysis involves receiving and verifying comprehensive information, exchanging views for review, evaluating credibility, and deeply analyzing intentions before placing trust in information.

papers.title: MACTS-EM: Multi-Agent Collaborative Time Series Forecasting with Emergent Memory
papers.abstract: Time series forecasting remains a critical challenge across numerous domains. Despite significant advancements, existing approaches struggle with complex phenomena such as regime shifts, cross-domain knowledge transfer, and multimodal data integration. This paper introduces Multi-Agent Collaborative Time Series Forecasting with Emergent Memory (MACTS-EM), a novel framework where specialised agents collaborate to achieve superior forecasting performance. The MACTS-EM architecture integrates: (1) domain-specialised forecasting agents for pattern recognition, anomaly detection, causal inference, and uncertainty quantification; (2) a meta-cognitive layer for dynamic agent allocation; (3) an emergent memory mechanism enabling cross-domain pattern transfer; (4) multimodal contextual integration; and (5) adversarial robustness components. Evaluation across financial markets, climate patterns, energy consumption, and pandemic propagation demonstrates that MACTS-EM outperforms existing approaches in most scenarios, with 8-12% improvement in forecasting accuracy, 22-27% better zero-shot transfer capability, 16-21% enhanced resilience during regime shifts, and 15-18% faster recovery after distribution shifts. Our findings suggest that collaborative, agentic approaches to time series forecasting represent a promising direction beyond traditional architectures, particularly for complex real-world scenarios requiring multi-resolution temporal understanding and contextual adaptation.

papers.title: Makerspaces in School Libraries - Transforming Learning Ecosystems for 21st Century Education: A review
papers.abstract: Makerspaces in school libraries have become transformative settings that enhance creativity, collaboration, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills in learners. Based on constructivist and constructionist theories, these spaces transition libraries from passive information stores to active learning environments. This review synthesizes existing research on the conceptual basis, implementation, educational effects, challenges, and future prospects of makerspaces, highlighting their role in supporting STEM/STEAM education, digital literacy, inquiry-based learning, and inclusive pedagogy. Global evidence, including guidelines from the American Association of School Librarians and the International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions, underscores the essential role of school librarians as facilitators and leaders in innovation. While studies indicate improved student engagement, self-directed learning, and collaborative knowledge construction, obstacles like funding shortages, training deficiencies, and sustainability challenges, particularly in developing areas, persist. The review concludes that makerspaces signify a paradigm shift in school librarianship, promoting 21st-century competencies and equitable access to creative technologies. To optimize their educational benefits, strategic planning, policy alignment, and librarian development are crucial.

papers.title: Comparative efficacy of platelet-rich fibrin matrix versus guided tissue regeneration membrane with DFDBA in immediate implant placement: A randomized controlled clinical trial
papers.abstract: Management of the peri-implant jumping distance remains challenging during immediate implant placement because inadequate bone fill may compromise osseointegration. This randomized trial included 30 systemically healthy patients receiving DFDBA with GTR membrane (n=15) or autologous PRFM (n=15) using a two-stage protocol. Plaque, gingival, bleeding, probing depth, attachment loss and crestal bone levels were assessed at baseline, 3 and 6 months and post-restoration. Both groups achieved 100% implant survival and success, with healthy probing depths and progressive reductions in plaque and gingival inflammation. No significant intergroup differences were observed, indicating comparable clinical outcomes with DFDBA combined with GTR membrane or PRFM.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed IIoT Digital Twin Framework for Automotive Cooling Predictive Maintenance and Odometer Fraud Detection using LSTM-Attention
papers.abstract: The shift to Industry 4.0 in the automotive industry requires an approach which moves away from passive monitoring and towards physics-based predictive maintenance. This paper introduces a Physics-Informed IIoT-Enabled Digital Twin (PI-DT) framework based on an Adaptive Physics-Informed Long Short-Term Memory with Attention (PI-LSTM-Attention) model to forecast the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of Engine Cooling Systems (ECS). The proposed architecture integrates the thermodynamic Monotonicity constraints into the learning process using Physics-Informed, meeting the 100% target of Monotonicity compliance, 99.64% Failure-Point Prediction Accuracy, and a self-healing rate of 0.00%. The framework is a Dual-Layer Edge-Cloud Continuum for ultra-low latency and complete offline operational resilience. In a Zero Trust cybersecurity paradigm, the accumulated ledgers of thermal damage are continually compared with the digital reading on the odometers to identify tamper and warranty fraud. The proposed PI-LSTM-Attention network is compared with Transformer architectures with lower latency and higher prediction accuracy, which proves its unique optimization for the automotive Edge, especially for time-critical applications.

papers.title: Chronologically Validated Explainable Machine Learning for Waterway Freight Forecasting in Vietnam
papers.abstract: Forecasting inland waterway freight is relevant to transport planning in Vietnam, where freight activity is characterized by high temporal persistence, spatial inequality, and socioeconomic heterogeneity. We developed an explainable, uncertainty-aware machine learning framework based on 147 observations from 49 provinces/cities during 2022-2024 and validated it chronologically. We used freight lags, lagged freight growth, population, population density, GRDP per capita, industrial production, and region as predictors. We compared seven regression models using 2022–2023 data for training and an independent chronological holdout of 2024 data for testing, plus province-grouped 5-fold cross-validation, permutation importance, SHAP analysis, conformal prediction, and target-transformation sensitivity. Extra Trees achieved the best chronological performance (R² = 0.992, RMSE = 1,656.5 kt, MAE = 767.9 kt, bias = −2.33%), followed by Gradient Boosting (R² = 0.990). SHAP analysis revealed that Freight lag 2 and Freight lag 1 were the most important predictors, contributing a mean absolute value of 5,912.2 kt and 5,535.4 kt, respectively. Direct-scale modeling performed better than log-transformed alternatives, and confidence intervals showed greater predictive uncertainty for very high-volume provinces. The results indicate that historical freight trends are the strongest predictor, and socioeconomic and regional factors add explanatory power. The approach combines predictive accuracy, interpretability, and uncertainty quantification, facilitating transparent identification of spatially differentiated freight-demand patterns across provinces and cities nationwide.

papers.title: 3D printing technologies in implantable medical devices: principles, applications, and cost-effectiveness in cardiovascular surgery
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) printing technologies, also known as additive manufacturing, have revolutionized biomedical engineering and surgical applications by enabling the high-accuracy and patient-specific production of complex geometries. Over the past decade, these technologies have moved beyond mere prototype manufacturing into routine clinical and industrial use. This review summarizes the fundamental operating principles, clinical applicability, advantages, and limitations of major 3D printing technologies, including SLA, FDM, selective laser sintering, selective laser melting, and binder jetting. Furthermore, their applications in cardiovascular and cardiac surgery, cost-effectiveness analyses, and future trends are discussed.

papers.title: KIDDO LEARN: DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTERACTIVE MULTIMEDIA LEARNING APPLICATION FOR CHILDREN’S LEARNING IN ENGLISH, MATHEMATICS AND SCIENCE
papers.abstract: The integration of multimedia technology into early childhood education has gained increasing attention due to its potential to create engaging and meaningful learning experiences for preschool children. However, many preschool classrooms continue to rely on teacher-centred instructional methods, such as worksheets and flashcards, which often fail to sustain children's attention, motivation, and active participation. In addition, existing educational applications frequently focus on a single learning domain and provide limited interactivity, restricting opportunities for holistic learning across multiple subjects. This study presents the design, development, and evaluation of Kiddo Learn, an interactive multimedia learning application that integrates English, Mathematics, and Science into a single curriculum-aligned platform for preschool education. The application was developed based on the I LEAP K2 Coursebooks to ensure alignment with preschool learning objectives and incorporates multimedia elements, including 2D animations, audio narration, colourful graphics, interactive games, quizzes, and immediate feedback to promote active learning. The application was developed using the ADDIE instructional design model, comprising the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation phases. Formative evaluation was conducted with three experts in multimedia and early childhood education to assess content accuracy, interface design, and usability, while summative evaluation involved fourteen kindergarten children aged five to six years to examine user engagement, ease of use, and learning experience. The evaluation results indicated that both experts and children responded positively to the application, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing learner engagement, motivation, usability, and interactive learning experiences. The findings suggest that integrating multiple learning domains within a curriculum-aligned multimedia application can support more meaningful preschool learning while complementing conventional classroom instruction. This study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on multimedia-assisted early childhood education by demonstrating the potential of interactive, child-centred learning applications to improve engagement and support holistic learning in preschool environments.

papers.title: Peningkatan Literasi Sains Siswa melalui Project-Based Learning pada Materi Bioteknologi: Studi Tindakan Kelas di SMP Islam As-Syakur Lendang Sepang
papers.abstract: This study investigates whether the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model can improve students’ scientific literacy in biotechnology and examines its implementation in ninth-grade science learning. This Classroom Action Research (CAR) was conducted in two cycles involving 12 ninth-grade students at SMP Islam As-Syakur Lendang Sepang. Each cycle consisted of planning, action, observation, and reflection. Data were collected through scientific literacy tests, learning implementation observations, scientific literacy observations, and questionnaires. The findings indicate that implementation of PjBL was fidelity reached, with student activity reaching 77.5% and teacher activity hitting 78.57% . Students’ scientific literacy improved from a pre-cycle average score of 44.41 to an N-Gain of 0.48 (medium) in the first cycle, and further increased to 0.71 (high) in the second cycle. Additionally, scientific literacy observations increased from 72.5% to 92.5%, while questionnaire results rose from 68.53% to 87.91%. These findings indicate that PjBL was associated with improved scientific literacy scores for strengthening scientific literacy in biotechnology. In conclusion, the implementation of project-based activities can promote active learning and support the development of students’ scientific literacy skills.

papers.abstract: This community service program aimed to optimize the learning process at MA Sabilal Muhtadin through the integration of interactive learning media, accessible educational technology, and active learning strategies. The program addressed teachers’ limited use of technology, limited variation in instructional methods, and students’ relatively low participation during classroom activities. The program was implemented through five stages: initial observation, program socialization, interactive media training, practice-based mentoring, and evaluation. The results indicated changes in teachers’ use of learning media, including the adoption of interactive presentations, educational videos, and simple visual media. Teachers also demonstrated improved ability to integrate media with discussion, collaboration, educational games, and presentations. These changes were accompanied by greater student participation and more conducive classroom interactions. The findings suggest that learning transformation was not primarily determined by the sophistication of technology, but by teachers’ capacity to integrate available resources with appropriate pedagogical strategies. The program therefore highlights the importance of practice-based and contextual mentoring for strengthening teachers’ digital-pedagogical capacity, particularly in educational institutions with limited infrastructure.

papers.title: DIGITAL TWIN AGGREGATES AND BIG DATA ANALYTICS FOR PREDICTIVE RISK MANAGEMENT IN CONTINUOUS MANUFACTURING: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
papers.abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology is a virtual representation of a physical asset, process or system that is continuously updated from operational data and is a key enabling technology for Industry 4.0 manufacturing research (Grieves andVickers, 2017; Kritzinger et al., 2018). Most of the current studies are related to the single asset, such as condition monitoring and fault diagnosis/predictive maintenance, using DTs (Tao et al., 2019; Tekinerdogan et al., 2021; Catal et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2023). The asset-level approach is not entirely appropriate for continuous manufacturing where machines and processes are highly inter-dependent and a disturbance at one step can make it to the flow, pressure, product quality and downstream processes. A way forward from asset level to system level risk prediction is through Digital Twin Aggregates (DTAs) that integrate information from several DTs into a system level view, along with big data analytics (Lu et al., 2020). While the implementation does have challenges of data integration, computational requirements, interoperability and standardisation (Shao and Helu, 2020; Perno, Hvam and Haug, 2022), these are heightened in resource-constrained, developing industrial economies (Muhla et al., 2025a; Mashava et al., 2026). This paper is a systematic literature review (SLR), performed following the PRISMA 2020 statement (Page et al., 2021) and the guidelines provided by Kitchenham and Charters (2007). Records published between January 2016 and September 2026 were obtained from Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and ScienceDirect and a total of 88 records were screened to identify 50 studies with an average quality score of 4.12 out of 5. All studies included were classified based on a multidimensional taxonomy of DT architecture, manufacturing level, data sources, analysis techniques, risk-management function, and validation environment. Among the 50 studies, there are 22 that are reviews or surveys, and only 19 that include empirical studies, 11 of which involve continuous or process manufacturing, and none of which have been validated with industrial data in a continuous process, in the case of multi-twin or aggregated architectures. The review summarizes existing applications, emerging technologies, and industrial implications, and identifies a research roadmap for practical, interoperable and system-level predictive risk management for continuous manufacturing.

papers.title: CYBER-PHYSICAL SECURITY FRAMEWORKS FOR INTEGRATED CAD/CAM AND DIGITAL TWIN WORKFLOWS: A STATE-OF-THE-ART SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
papers.abstract: Integrated computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM), product lifecycle management (PLM) and industrial control and digital-twin platforms provide a continuity from design to production, enhancing traceability, but they also enable an impersonated identity, model, toolpath, software component or sensor stream to travel through the entire workflow. The review brings together 56 peer-reviewed articles and six normative sources, most of which were from the period 2016 to September 2026. OpenAlex, publisher records (as retrieved from Crossref) and backward citation chaining were processed through a PRISMA 2020-driven workflows, and evidence was coded by workflow stage, asset, threat, security objective, control family, and validation strength. Network intrusion, theft or tampering of CAD models, manipulation of CAM parameters and post-processors, falsification of a digital-twin state, insecure cloud collaboration, supply-chain compromise, and unsafe shop-floor commands are the main threats. There are seven families of published countermeasures: standards-based governance, identity-centred access control, segmentation, verifiable provenance, blockchain-backed traceability, watermarking and fingerprinting, and twin-assisted anomaly detection. No family is big enough: source data were not necessarily correct; anomaly detection was based on representative data; and conventional IT controls under-represented operational safety and timing. Due to the influence of process parameters on part quality, such as feed rate, injection pressure or infill density, small, unauthorized changes to the process can result in parts that are defective but appear plausible. As such, a lifecycle defence-in-depth approach is proposed, featuring ownership of artefacts, trust boundaries, a signed manufacturing job package, least privilege, monitored hand-offs, process-aware detection and verified recovery. Future work should validate integrated frameworks on realistic CAD-to-machine testbeds, such as learning factories, and report the outcomes of security, production, safety and recovery in a combined manner.

papers.abstract: 성과 관리에서 피드백은 핵심적인 역할을 하지만, 그 효과는 상황에 따라 일관되지 않게 나타난다. 본 연구는 피드백 개입 이론, 확장-구축 이론, 사회 역할 이론을 바탕으로 미래 지향적 피드백, 심리적 안전감, 성별이 능동적 학습행동과 직무 성과에 미치는 영향을 분석했다. 국내 다양한 산업에 종사하는 정규직 근로자 250명을 대상으로 두 시점에 걸쳐 수집한 설문 조사 자료를 분석한 결과, 심리적 안전감이 높은 경우 미래지향적 피드백이 능동적 학습 행동을 촉진하는 것으로 나타났다. 특히, 심리적 안전감이 낮은 환경에서는 남성 직원의 경우 미래지향적 피드백이 오히려 능동적 학습 행동을 저해하는 부적 관계가 나타난 반면, 여성 직원에게서는 이러한 부적 관계가 관찰되지 않아, 심리적 안전감이 성별과 함께 작용하는 삼원상호작용의 경향이 나타났다. 또한 능동적 학습 행동은 이러한 상호작용이 직무 성과로 이어지는 매개 경로로 기능할 가능성을 확인했다. 본 연구는 미래지향적 피드백의 효과가 조직 맥락과 구성원의 성별에 따라 달라질 수 있음을 실증적으로 규명함으로써 피드백 개입 이론과 사회 역할 이론의 통합적 적용 가능성을 확장하고, 조직이 구성원의 특성을 고려한 차별화된 피드백 전략을 설계하는 데 실무적 시사점을 제공한다.

papers.title: Activity Cliffs and Machine Learning Generalization in QSAR: Why Similar Molecules Remain Difficult to Predict
papers.abstract: Machine learning has substantially expanded the predictive capability of quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, yet reliable generalization remains difficult in chemically challenging regions. Activity cliffs-pairs of highly similar molecules that exhibit large differences in biological activity-represent a particularly stringent test because they violate the local smoothness assumed by many similarity-based and representation-learning approaches. This narrative review examines why activity cliffs remain difficult for contemporary QSAR models and how they expose limitations that may be concealed by conventional global performance metrics. We discuss the definition, detection, and chemical origins of activity cliffs; their relationship to discontinuities in structure-activity landscapes; and the influence of molecular representation, training-test partitioning, structural redundancy, and data leakage on apparent model performance. Evidence from fingerprint-based machine learning, deep neural networks, graph neural networks, and recent molecular foundation models indicates that increasing model complexity does not consistently resolve activity-cliff prediction. Models with strong overall QSAR performance may still exhibit substantially larger errors or poor sensitivity for cliff-forming compounds. Recent approaches that explicitly incorporate activity-cliff information through pairwise, contrastive, or activity-aware representation learning provide a promising alternative to conventional compound-level regression. We therefore propose an activity-cliff-aware QSAR perspective integrating rigorous bioactivity curation, activity-landscape characterization, leakage-resistant validation, global and cliff-specific evaluation, applicability-domain analysis, uncertainty quantification, and cliff-aware learning objectives. Activity cliffs should ultimately be regarded not merely as problematic outliers, but as information-rich stress tests of molecular machine-learning generalization and local structure-activity understanding.

papers.title: Temporal Consistency-Based Data Selection for Active Learning in Construction Site Object Detection
papers.abstract: Continuous construction-site video monitoring requires object detectors that adapt to changing site conditions under limited annotation budgets.This study proposes an Interpolation query that selects frames containing potential missed detections by matching and interpolating bounding boxes from surrounding frames.The query was incorporated into active learning and compared with random sampling using ten days of video from a single construction site under equal daily frame budgets.Frame hit rates were approximately 63.0-99.0%,and proposal box precision was approximately 50-88%.Although its advantage over random sampling was not sustained on the cumulative evaluation dataset, the method achieved higher next-day mAP50 in seven of ten transitions, with a maximum gain of 7.5 percentage points.These findings suggest that temporal consistency-based sampling of potential missed detections may improve next-day generalization under limited annotation budgets.
papers.first_author_affiliation: Department of Civil Engineering , Hongik University ,
papers.venue: Journal of Construction Automation and Robotics

papers.title: Physics-informed Perceiver IO: Scalable mesh-free solving of partial differential equations without supervision
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a powerful framework for solving partial differential equations by incorporating governing equations into the training objective. Recent advances have improved their robustness and applicability across a broad range of scientific and engineering problems. Nevertheless, efficiently learning multiscale or highly oscillatory solution structures while maintaining computational scalability remains an active area of research. Transformer-based variants provide a promising mechanism for modeling global interactions, but their use of full self-attention substantially increases computational and memory requirements. These considerations motivate the development of more computationally efficient attention-based architectures for physics-informed learning. In this work, we propose the Physics-Informed Perceiver IO (PIP-IO), a mesh-free framework for PDE learning that adapts the attention-based Perceiver IO architecture to physics-informed learning. Instead of applying self-attention directly to all collocation points, PIP-IO employs a latent cross-attention mechanism that first aggregates information into a compact shared latent representation and then predicts the solution at arbitrary query locations from this representation. This design considerably improves computational efficiency for large-scale problems while conditioning the latent representation on the given problem specification. The governing PDE is enforced through the standard physics-informed residual computed from the decoded solution which requires no additional physics constraint in the latent space. The proposed method is assessed on a diverse collection of elliptic and time-dependent problems, including multiscale Poisson, heterogeneous-coefficient Poisson, Helmholtz, convection, wave, and Burgers equations, together with a composability study on the chaotic Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation. Under a unified experimental protocol, PIP-IO consistently achieves competitive or improved accuracy compared with representative MLP- and Transformer-based PINN architectures while consuming less GPU memory than PINNsFormer. These results show that PIP-IO offers an efficient and robust framework for scalable physics-informed PDE learning.

papers.title: EKSPLORASI PENGGUNAAN GAMIFIKASI SEBAGAI PENDEKATAN PEMBELAJARAN AKTIF DALAM SUBJEK MATEMATIK SEKOLAH RENDAH: EKSPLORASI PENGGUNAAN GAMIFIKASI SEBAGAI PENDEKATAN PEMBELAJARAN AKTIF DALAM SUBJEK MATEMATIK SEKOLAH RENDAH
papers.abstract: Pendekatan pembelajaran aktif penting dalam membangunkan kemahiran Pendidikan Abad ke-21 (PAK21) bagi subjek Matematik sekolah rendah. Namun demikian, pengajaran berpusatkan guru dan kaedah tradisional masih banyak diamalkan di bilik darjah. Oleh itu, kajian kualitatif berbentuk eksploratori ini dijalankan bagi meneroka amalan guru Matematik sekolah rendah terhadap penggunaan elemen gamifikasi sebagai pendekatan pembelajaran aktif. Kajian melibatkan enam orang guru Matematik di daerah Gombak, Selangor yang dipilih secara persampelan bertujuan. Data dikumpulkan melalui temu bual separa berstruktur, pemerhatian bilik darjah dan analisis dokumen kemudian dianalisis menggunakan analisis tematik. Dapatan kajian menunjukkan bahawa penggunaan elemen gamifikasi seperti kuiz interaktif, sistem ganjaran dan pertandingan berkumpulan didapati berpotensi meningkatkan minat, motivasi, keyakinan diri serta penglibatan aktif murid. Walau bagaimanapun, beberapa cabaran dikenal pasti seperti kekangan masa, keterbatasan teknologi dan perbezaan tahap kebolehan murid. Implikasi kajian menunjukkan bahawa gamifikasi berpotensi membantu guru mewujudkan suasana pembelajaran Matematik yang lebih interaktif, menyeronokkan dan berpusatkan murid. Secara keseluruhannya, kajian ini menunjukkan bahawa gamifikasi mampu menjadi pendekatan yang berkesan dalam memperkukuh pedagogi Matematik sekolah rendah apabila dilaksanakan secara sistematik dan fleksibel. Active learning approaches are essential for developing 21st-century learning skills among primary school pupils, particularly in Mathematics education. Nevertheless, teacher-centred instruction and traditional teaching methods remain widely practised in classrooms. Therefore, this exploratory qualitative study was conducted to explore primary school Mathematics teachers’ practices in using gamification elements as an active learning approach. The study involved six Mathematics teachers from the Gombak district, Selangor, who were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, classroom observations and document analysis, and subsequently analysed using thematic analysis. The findings indicate that the use of gamification elements, such as interactive quizzes, reward systems and group competitions, has the potential to enhance pupils’ interest, motivation, self-confidence and active participation in Mathematics learning. However, several challenges were identified, including time constraints, limited access to technology and differences in pupils’ ability levels. The findings further suggest that gamification can support teachers in creating a more interactive, enjoyable and learner-centred Mathematics learning environment. Overall, this study demonstrates that gamification has the potential to serve as an effective pedagogical approach for strengthening primary Mathematics education when implemented systematically and flexibly.

papers.title: Strategi Active Learning dalam Menciptakan Suasana yang Kondusif pada Kelas IV Tahfizh di MIS Nurussalam Deli Tua
papers.abstract: This study aims to describe and analyze active learning strategies applied by tahfizh teachers in creating a conducive learning atmosphere in Grade IV at Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Swasta (MIS) Nurussalam Deli Tua. The often monotonous and less varied tahfizh learning conditions form the background for the importance of implementing active learning strategies so that students can memorize the Qur'an optimally in an enjoyable, active, and meaningful learning environment. This study employed a qualitative research method with a descriptive approach. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation. The results show that: (1) Tahfizh teachers in Grade IV of MIS Nurussalam Deli Tua apply various active learning strategies such as paired listening (sima'i), interactive talaqqi, rotating muraja'ah, tahfizh moving class, reward-based memorization, and small group discussion; (2) The implemented active learning strategies have proven effective in creating a conducive atmosphere characterized by increased enthusiasm, concentration, and motivation for memorization; (3) Supporting factors include teacher competence, principal support, adequate facilities, and a religious madrasa environment; (4) Inhibiting factors include differences in students' memorization ability, limited learning time, and lack of parental support at home.

papers.title: Improving Cognitive Engagement and Achievement in Biology through PBL: A Mixed Methods Exploration
papers.abstract: This study investigates the impact of Problem-Based Learning (PBL) on enhancing student understanding of high school biology, specifically focusing on the topic of biodiversity. This research is grounded in constructivist and inquirybased pedagogical theory, addressing common issues of low engagement and underachievement in biology classrooms. As Maldivian schools transition toward more active learning paradigms, this study offers timely insight into how studentcentered strategies such as PBL might improve both comprehension and motivation. A mixed methods approach was used, involving a single Grade 12 student selected through purposive sampling. Quantitative data were gathered using pre- and posttests to measure changes in conceptual understanding and engagement. Qualitative data emerged from interviews, reflective discussions, and analysis of student work. The results showed improved student performance, with a 20% increase in posttest scores. The participant demonstrated an enhanced ability to apply biological concepts in unfamiliar contexts. Beyond academic gains, the PBL strategy also fostered metacognitive skills, critical thinking, and development of transferable skills. Student reflections highlighted increased engagement and a deeper connection to the learning process. Despite the single-subject scope and limited sample size, the findings provide compelling evidence supporting the effectiveness of PBL in promoting meaningful, student-centered learning in biology classrooms. The study suggests broader implementation of PBL in Maldivian classrooms and contributes to the literature advocating innovative, inquiry-based approaches in science instruction.

papers.abstract: This research aimed to: (1) investigate the background information, current conditions, desired conditions, and priority needs for developing teachers’ active learning management competencies through the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and professional learning communities (PLCs) to enhance student quality at Khok Si Wittayasan School; and (2) develop, implement, and evaluate a model for enhancing teachers’ active learning management competencies through the integration of artificial intelligence and professional learning communities to improve student quality at Khok Si Wittayasan School. This study employed a research and development (R&D) approach and was conducted from the second semester of the 2024 academic year to the first semester of the 2025 academic year. The target group consisted of school administrators, teachers, and 491 students in Grades 7–12 at Khok Si Wittayasan School. The research instruments included questionnaires, interview forms, the developed model and its implementation manual, a model evaluation form, a knowledge and understanding test, an active learning management competency assessment form, satisfaction questionnaires, and student quality development records. Data were collected through surveys, expert interviews, and a one-group pretest–posttest implementation of the model. The data were analyzed using percentage, mean, standard deviation, the Modified Priority Needs Index (PNImodified), the Wilcoxon Signed-Ranks Test, and content analysis. The findings revealed that: 1) the overall current condition of teachers’ active learning management was at a moderate level (μ = 2.54, = 0.58), whereas the overall desired condition was at the highest level (μ = 4.57, = 0.58), with an overall PNImodified of 0.80 2) the developed model, designated the AIPHR2S Model, comprised six components: principles, objectives, a six-step development process, support systems, conditions for success, and measurement and evaluation. Following the implementation of the model, teachers’ knowledge and understanding were significantly higher than their pre-development scores at the .01 level. Their overall active learning management competency was at the highest level, with an average score of 84.33%. All teachers successfully developed best practices, accounting for 100%. The model was evaluated as having the highest levels of appropriateness and usefulness. Both teachers and students reported the highest level of satisfaction with the model. Furthermore, student quality improved in terms of academic achievement, desirable characteristics, and key competencies.

papers.title: Directed growth of bacterial nanocellulose in constructal scaffolds
papers.abstract: Bacterial nanocellulose is a strong, highly crystalline and biodegradable biopolymer, but its use has stayed largely confined to flat sheets. Its potential as a three-dimensional design material remains untested. This research investigates how the geometry of a solid scaffold directs where the material forms. Within a material-driven design framework, we combined hands-on exploration with parametrically defined channels, bio-inspired flow architectures and porous gyroid lattices. We followed growth in situ by time-lapse imaging under static batch feeding. Scaffold geometry influenced deposition through capillary transport at the air-liquid interface. Below a critical channel width of about 1 to 1.3 mm, capillary rise lifted and destabilised the interface, producing uneven, vertically inclined pellicles and trapped fluid pockets. Highly permeable architectures suppressed capillary rise, held the interface flat and gave uniform colonisation. Scaffolds of 10% solidity reached a mean cellulose area fraction of 65 ± 3.7%, compared with 7.0 ± 1.6% at 40% solidity. Geometry is therefore an active design parameter that determines where cellulose grows, and it offers a route to programming grown composites through physical boundary conditions rather than through post-growth assembly.

papers.title: 3D PRINTING IN PERSONALIZED MEDICINE FOR MUSCULOSKELETAL DISORDERS: CURRENT TECHNOLOGIES, CLINICAL APPLICATION AND LIMITATIONS – A REVIEW
papers.abstract: 3D printing technologies are playing an increasingly important role in the development of personalized medicine, particularly in the treatment of musculoskeletal disorders. Their application enables the fabrication of structures tailored to the individual anatomical conditions of patients, which may contribute to improved clinical outcomes and therapeutic effectiveness. The aim of this review article is to present the current state of knowledge regarding the application of 3D printing technologies in orthopedics and reconstructive surgery, with particular emphasis on additive manufacturing techniques, biomaterials, and their clinical applications. A literature review was conducted using the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases, including publications from 2018 to 2025 related to additive manufacturing, orthopedics, tissue engineering, and bioprinting. The review discusses the main additive manufacturing techniques, including fused deposition modelling (FDM), stereolithography (SLA), selective laser sintering (SLS), and metal-based technologies such as selective laser melting (SLM) and direct metal laser sintering (DMLS), analysing their properties, advantages, and limitations. Particular attention is given to clinical applications, including anatomical models for preoperative planning, patient-specific implants and prostheses, as well as the use of 3D printing in tissue engineering and bioprinting. Available evidence suggests that 3D printing technologies may improve surgical precision, reduce operative time, and support bone tissue regeneration through the fabrication of structures with controlled porosity and optimized mechanical properties. At the same time, important limitations remain, including high implementation costs, lack of process standardization, regulatory challenges, and the limited number of long-term clinical studies. In conclusion, 3D printing technologies represent a promising tool in the advancement of personalized medicine and modern orthopedic treatment. However, their broader implementation in clinical practice requires further high-quality clinical research, development of standardized manufacturing protocols, and continued progress in biomaterials and regenerative medicine, patient-specific implants.

papers.title: 3D-printed Ti6Al4V alloy by selective laser melting: a study of surface quality, dimensional accuracy, and mechanical characteristics
papers.abstract: In this study, essential characteristics of selective laser melting (SLM)-printed parts (surface quality, mechanical properties, and dimensional accuracy) were evaluated simultaneously for potential practical applications. Parts were fabricated using industrially validated processing parameters recommended by the machine manufacturer to establish a comprehensive baseline assessment of manufacturing quality. Surface topography measurements showed relatively high surface roughness (Sa 8.60 µm, Sz 70.34 µm), mainly due to inherent SLM process characteristics. Compared to wrought Ti6Al4V, the fabricated Ti6Al4V exhibited higher tensile strength. The hardness of the printed parts (37.5 ± 1.1 HRC) suggests good wear resistance. Dimensional analysis revealed deviations ranging from approximately −25 µm to −200 µm, corresponding mainly to tolerance grades IT9-IT12. The roundness was in the range of 25 - 50 µm, while the coaxiality was approximately 27.7 µm. These results provide useful insights into the quality and limitations of SLM-printed Ti6Al4V parts for further investigation.

papers.title: ENHANCING THE BIOCOMPATIBILITY OF 3D PRINTED TITANIUM IMPLANTS BY MICROPLASMA SPRAYING OF HYDROXYAPATITE COATINGS
papers.abstract: The growing demand for durable and biologically functional orthopedic implants has stimulated the development of surface-modification strategies capable of improving tissue integration while limiting bacterial colonization. In this study, porous Ti6Al4V scaffolds produced by additive manufacturing were functionalized with hydroxyapatite (HAP) using robotic microplasma spraying, and their biological performance was evaluated in comparison with gas-abrasive-treated Ti6Al4V surfaces. Surface morphology and elemental composition were examined by scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM–EDX). Cytocompatibility was assessed using rat bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells, with metabolic activity quantified by the Alamar Blue assay, while antibacterial performance was evaluated against Escherichia coli. HAP deposition markedly altered the interaction of the titanium surface with both mammalian and bacterial cells. The coated scaffolds supported greater MSC metabolic activity and more extensive cellular attachment than the uncoated Ti6Al4V reference, with cell viability increasing by 56%. At the same time, E. coli proliferation was suppressed, with bacterial growth approximately 30% lower after 15 h of incubation. These findings demonstrate that microplasma-deposited HAP can provide additively manufactured titanium scaffolds with a favorable combination of cytocompatibility and resistance to bacterial growth. The integration of additive manufacturing with controlled plasma-based surface functionalization therefore represents a promising approach for the development of porous titanium implants with improved biological performance.

papers.title: Infinite-Dimensional Closed-Loop Inverse Kinematics for Soft Robots via Neural Operators
papers.abstract: For fully actuated rigid robots, kinematic inversion is a purely geometric problem, efficiently solved by closed-loop inverse kinematics (CLIK) schemes that compute joint configurations to position the robot body in space. For underactuated soft robots, however, not all configurations are attainable through control action, making kinematic inversion extremely challenging. Extensions of CLIK address this by introducing end-to-end mappings from actuation to task space for the controller to operate on, but typically assume finite dimensions of the underlying virtual configuration space. In this work, we formulate CLIK in the infinite-dimensional domain to reason about the entire soft robot shape while solving tasks. We do this by composing an actuation-to-shape map with a shape-to-task map, deriving the differential end-to-end kinematics via an infinite-dimensional chain rule, and thereby obtaining a Jacobian-based CLIK algorithm. Since this actuation-to-shape mapping is rarely available in closed form, we propose to learn it using differentiable neural operator networks. We first present an analytical study on a constant-curvature segment, and then apply the neural version of the algorithm to a three-fiber soft robotic arm whose underlying model relies on morphoelasticity and active filament theory.

papers.title: Effect of build platform location and part spacing on microstructure and mechanical properties of Ti-6Al-4V fabricated by electron beam powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: Electron beam powder bed fusion (EB-PBF) is a metal additive manufacturing (AM) technology widely used to produce Ti-6Al-4V components. In industrial batch production, parts are typically arranged with minimal spacing to maximize productivity; however, the effects of build platform location and part spacing on part properties remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the influence of build platform location and part spacing on the microstructure and mechanical properties of EB-PBF Ti-6Al-4V. Tensile test samples were fabricated at three different locations (center, middle, and corner) and three different part spacings (5, 7.5, and 10 mm). Tensile and hardness tests were performed, α lath thickness was measured using an optical microscope, and one-way ANOVA was conducted to evaluate statistical significance. The results showed that yield strength (YS) and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) increased from the center to the corner of the build platform and with increasing part spacing. These improvements were associated with thinner α lath thickness; that is, the thinner the α lath thickness, the higher the strength. In contrast, elongation at fracture (EL) and hardness showed no simple correlation with α lath thickness. Depending on build platform location and part spacing, YS, UTS, EL, and hardness varied by 1.3–2.3%, 0.8–1.9%, 4.6–13.2%, and 1.9–4.1%, respectively. Overall, build platform location primarily affected ductility, whereas part spacing mainly affected strength. These findings guide optimizing part layout in EB-PBF manufacturing and improve the understanding of how build platform location and part spacing influence microstructure and mechanical properties.

papers.title: Penerapan Model Project Based Learning (PJBL) Melalui Media Manipulasi untuk Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar Siswa pada Mata Pelajaran Matematika Materi Bangun Ruang Kelas 2 di SDN Jrebeng Kulon 1 Kota Probolinggo
papers.abstract: This research was motivated by the low ability of second-grade students at SD Negeri Jrebeng Kulon I, Probolinggo City, to understand three-dimensional shapes in mathematics learning. This study aimed to determine the learning process and students’ learning outcomes through the implementation of the Project Based Learning (PjBL) model assisted by Manipulative media. The research method used was Classroom Action Research (CAR), which was conducted in two cycles consisting of planning, implementation, observation, and reflection. The research subjects were 20 second-grade students of SD Negeri Jrebeng Kulon I, Probolinggo City. Data collection techniques were carried out through observation, interviews, pre-tests and post-tests, and documentation. The results showed that the implementation of the Project Based Learning (PjBL) model assisted by Manipulative media could improve students’ learning outcomes in three-dimensional shapes in mathematics learning. The students’ average score increased from 69.50 in the first cycle to 82.25 in the second cycle. The percentage of learning mastery also increased from 55% to 100%. In addition, students became more active and enthusiastic during the learning process. The implementation of project-based learning with concrete media provided a more active learning experience and helped students understand three-dimensional shape concepts through real activities. These findings indicate that the integration of the PjBL model and Manipulative media can support mathematics learning in elementary schools.

papers.title: EFFECT OF ZINC ACETATE CONCENTRATION IN A CA(H₂PO₂)₂–ZN(CH₃COO)₂ ELECTROLYTE ON THE STRUCTURE AND PROPERTIES OF PEO COATINGS ON ADDITIVELY MANUFACTURED TI-6AL-4V ALLOY
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effect of the concentration of zinc acetate (Zn(CH₃COO)₂) in a calcium hypophosphite (Ca(H₂PO₂)₂) electrolyte on the formation and properties of coatings produced by plasma electrolytic oxidation on Ti-6Al-4V alloy manufactured by selective laser melting. The plasma electrolytic oxidation process was carried out under constant conditions, while the Zn(CH₃COO)₂ concentration was varied within the range of 0.1-0.4 mol/L. The coating morphology, elemental composition, phase structure, thickness were studied using light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction. The mechanical properties of the coatings were characterized by microhardness and wear resistance tests. Zinc acetate was found to significantly affect the growth and structure of the oxide layers. With increasing Zn(CH₃COO)₂ concentration, the coating thickness increased from 1.51 ± 0.26 to 5.21 ± 1.27 μm, the zinc content in the surface layer increased, and the morphology changed from an open porous structure to a denser one. According to X-ray diffraction analysis, the titanium substrate made the main contribution to the diffraction patterns, whereas the Ca- and Zn-containing components were in an amorphous, poorly crystalline, or nanodispersed state. The best tribological properties, including the lowest coefficient of friction, were obtained at 0.2 mol/L Zn(CH₃COO)₂. A further increases in Zn(CH₃COO)₂ concentration result in greater coating heterogeneity and reduced microhardness of the substrate-coating composite. The results confirm the possibility of controlled modification of plasma electrolytic oxidation coatings for medical applications.

summary_zh.motivation: 为改善增材制造Ti-6Al-4V植入体的表面生物活性与耐磨性。
summary_zh.method: 在Ca(H₂PO₂)₂电解液中改变醋酸锌浓度，对SLM Ti-6Al-4V进行等离子体电解氧化处理。
summary_zh.result: 锌浓度升高使涂层增厚、结构致密，0.2 mol/L时摩擦系数最低，过高浓度导致涂层不均和硬度下降。
summary_zh.validation: 采用SEM-EDS、XRD、显微硬度与磨损试验表征涂层。

summary_en.motivation: To tailor the surface bioactivity and tribological performance of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V implants.
summary_en.method: Plasma electrolytic oxidation was performed on SLM Ti-6Al-4V in a calcium hypophosphite electrolyte with varying zinc acetate concentrations.
summary_en.result: Increasing zinc acetate thickened and densified the coating, with the lowest friction coefficient at 0.2 mol/L, while higher concentrations caused heterogeneity and reduced composite microhardness.
summary_en.validation: Coatings were characterized by SEM-EDS, XRD, microhardness, and wear resistance testing.
